````md
- NVIDIA 官网素材(firecrawl/浏览器下载):RTX PRO 产品图与参数、NVLink/IB/Spectrum-X 官方拓扑图、CDU 液冷图;全部记入 assets/manifest.yaml(URL+日期)

### 阶段 4:18 页内容逐页落地(蓝图速览)
- **p1** 建设目标:左侧四组要点(定位/负载与瓶颈:Agent 长上下文→KV与带宽、coding→长输出、RAG→prefill 重/服务形式/SLA 三指标);右侧模型卡片列(4 文本模型标总参/激活/ctx/许可,H3 作多模态扩展角标);底部「新模型 T+N 天上线」能力带
- **p2** 上:Token Factory 三层概念图(原生 shapes:算力存储网络→model serving→SLA token 交付,右侧 4 增长驱动箭头);下:产能盘(3×1亿 tpm)+ 投产时间线甘特条 + 5 年营收/利润曲线(matplotlib)+ **公式框进 slide** + 变量表
- **p3** 整体架构:六横层(应用/全球流量调度 cluster 级/API 网关路由 worker 级/推理 Serving SGLang·vLLM·Dynamo/资源层/基础设施)+ 四纵柱(安全/可观测/性能仿真评估/Planner 扩缩容)+ k8s 平台;左下贴 cluster-facility-planes 截图作资源层实景锚点;按 A5 调研纠偏命名
- **p4** 推理服务逻辑架构:API GW → cache/load-aware Router → 多 model worker pool → prefill/decode 分离 → TP/PP/EP(DeepEP)+ 多级 KV(HBM→DRAM→NVMe);每环节挂影响指标标签(TTFT/TPOT/吞吐/成本);右栏技术点清单:continuous batching、chunked prefill、agg vs disagg、量化 FP8/FP4、MTP→DSpark、DCP、KV offload;**notes 重头**:每技术点收益/代价/适用/不适用场景
- **p5** 容量规划:显存构成堆叠条(权重/KV/开销/安全系数,旁注 K3 与 V4 新注意力口径)+ 容量推导链公式;下半 scale-up 阶梯图(1 GPU 288GB→HGX 8 卡 2.3TB TP→NVL72 20TB TP+EP→再 scale-out PP/EP),贴 hgx-board + gb300-rack 截图
- **p5-1/2/3** worked-example 三段式(输入表→计算过程→输出 worker 形态),数字全部由 capacity_model.py 生成;对标公开部署配置(vLLM recipe/NIM)
- **p6** 四平台对比表:RTX PRO(官网图)/HGX B300/GB300 NVL72/Vera Rubin(模拟器截图);行:核心参数(模拟器 keySpecs)/可跑模型/扩展方式/机房门槛/参考成本(区间+来源)/交付周期/性能口径
- **p7** 网络:NVIDIA 官方 scale-up/scale-out 拓扑图为主视觉 + 部件参数表(NVLink/NVSwitch/CX-8/IB X800/Spectrum-X leaf-spine)+ 「支撑场景→影响指标」列(EP all-to-all→TPOT、KV 迁移→TTFT);N-S/Storage/OOB 各一行带过
- **p8** 存储(设计提案):「数据生命周期泳道图」——横轴推理业务动线(模型分发→加载→运行时→归档→RAG 检索),四泳道(本地 NVMe/高性能共享/对象存储/DB+向量库),每泳道标职责/位置/关键参数/影响指标(模型冷启动→新模型上线承诺、RAG 检索时延→端到端 TTFT)
- **p9** 机房电力液冷:按 p6 四平台列硬门槛(GB300 142kW→必须 DLC、CDU 水温、承重、周期、$/MW)+ 冷却/电力平面截图 + 官网 CDU 图
- **p10** 运维:场景×角色矩阵(发布/扩缩容/故障定位/性能回归/安全审计/成本优化 × SRE/推理工程师/平台/安全/FinOps),标 L0-L4 自动化程度,**AI agent 可承担的格子高亮**,notes 给依据
- **p11** PoC 与验收:原生 shapes 流程图(需求对齐→workload 画像→环境→基准测试(定 SLA 找最大 goodput)→SLA 验证→故障演练→验收);常见坑框(只测峰值不看 goodput、prompt 分布失真、cache 命中虚高、烤机不足)
- **p11-1/2/3** PoC 实例:输入信息项(QPS、长度分布、cache 特征)→必测输出(吞吐-延迟曲线、P95 TTFT/TPOT、单位成本、恢复时间)→假设示例数据表,与 p5-x worker 形态一致形成「规划→验证」闭环
- **p12** 四象限:BOM 摘要(来自 calc)/TCO 五年条形/风险 Top5(交期、价格波动、模型迭代重规划、许可合规、SLA 违约)/路线图愿景收尾(2026 文本 token 工厂→2027 多模态→Agent 原生平台,「从卖 token 到卖结果」)

### 阶段 5:构建、检查、交付
1. `python build.py` 出 out/aifactory-deck-v1.pptx
2. `check/lint_deck.py`:每页 notes 非空、来源角标非空、字号≥12pt、文本不超版式预算
3. `check/render_pdf.sh`:soffice headless → PDF → 逐页 PNG,自查溢出错位(LibreOffice 中文渲染仅作 lint,最终视觉以 PowerPoint/Keynote 打开为准)
4. SendUserFile 交付 pptx + 逐页预览 PNG;列出所有「待用户拍板」参数清单(含 tpm 另一口径对照)

## 关键参考文件
- `src/lib/roofline.ts`、`src/lib/capacity.ts` — capacity_model.py 的口径与 null 纪律移植源
- `src/data/models.ts` — 模型参数 dict 的结构范式
- `src/data/hgx-b300.ts` 等 keySpecs — p5/p6 硬件参数唯一来源(模拟器数据可溯源)
- `src/lib/palette.ts` — 主题色提取
- `tests/e2e/factory.spec.ts` — 截图清单与深链补拍参考
- `sources/` 券商 PDF — GB300 成本交叉背书

## 风险与 Fallback(要点)
- GB300 无官方价 → 区间+中值+敏感性,明注第三方估算
- 稀疏注意力 KV 精确口径查不到 → null 纪律,给上下界+假设标注
- 利润可能为负 → 盈亏平衡叙事,不做单点结论
- LibreOffice 渲染偏差 → 只做溢出 lint;python-pptx 不嵌字体 → 字体名参数化
- p3/p4 手绘照片、RTX PRO 模拟器补全、H3 视频产能模型 → 均为已知的 v2 迭代项

## 验证
- 616 项现有模拟器测试不受影响(deck/ 不触碰 src/)
- calc 脚本带自检:公式量纲检查、与 roofline.ts 对同一输入(deepseek-v3)的输出交叉核对
- 最终 pptx 逐页渲染 PNG 人工/agent 过一遍 + 交付用户评审;评审意见回流迭代
````

```text
## Approved Plan:
# AI Factory Solution Deck v1(12+6 页 PPTX)实施计划

## Context

用户(AI 基础设施售前架构师)需要一版「推理型 AI Factory 解决方案」deck:12 主页 + 6 附属页(5-1/2/3 容量实例、11-1/2/3 PoC 实例),第一版定框架,后续按客户场景快速迭代定制。内容覆盖:建设目标与 SLA、产能规划与 5 年财务测算、整体/推理服务架构、容量规划方法、计算平台选型、网络、存储、机房电力液冷、运维、PoC 验收、BOM/TCO/路线图。

**已与用户确认的决策**:
1. 交付格式:**原生 PPTX**(python-pptx + 统一模板),16:9,中文为主、术语保留英文,每页有演讲者备注(notes)
2. **浅色商务风**主题;模拟器深色截图加卡片/边框处理
3. page6 的 RTX PRO 用 NVIDIA 官网素材(模拟器不补,留作后续任务);其余三平台用模拟器截图
4. page3/4 用户手绘照片暂缺,按其文字描述先做(diagram 节点结构留好,便于照片到位后对照修正)
5. 定价口径:海外 token 工厂(Fireworks)美元价;GB300 用美国第三方参考价($3.5–6.5M/rack,中值 $4.5M,标注「第三方估算」)
6. 「1 亿 tpm」= **总吞吐(prefill+decode)**;营收按输入:输出比(默认 4:1)拆分计价,notes 放另一口径对照

**计划期已核实的关键事实**(执行期直接引用,不重查):
- Fireworks **无公开统一 SLA**(企业按 MSA 协商;第三方监测 uptime ~99.8%)→ p1 措辞改为「对齐头部 token 工厂可观测口径:P95 TTFT / P95 TPOT / 月可用性 99.9% 起」,notes 注明这反而是差异化机会
- Fireworks 定价(每百万 token 输入/输出):GLM 5.2 $1.40/$4.40、DeepSeek V4 Pro $1.74/$3.48(cached $0.145)、V4 Flash $0.14/$0.28;cached/batch 5 折;2026-09 起 US serverless 有 50% 溢价(主口径用全球价)
- 模型架构:GLM-5.2 753B/40B active MoE 稀疏注意力;GLM-5.3 同底座 post-train 升级;Kimi K3 2.8T/104B,**KDA(常数状态)+ gated MLA 混合,69:24 层**——用户「KDA+MLA 影响 KV 口径」判断正确;DeepSeek V4 Pro 1.6T/49B、Flash 284B/13B,CSA 稀疏注意力(1M ctx 下 KV 约传统 10%)
- **MiniMax-H3 实为 33B 视频生成模型(非文本 LLM),且许可排除美欧英韩** → p1 列为「多模态扩展路线」而非产能主力(用户本来也未给 H3 配 tpm,自洽)
- 「MTP 的 DSpark」**真实存在**(arXiv 2607.05147,NVIDIA Megatron Bridge 有官方文档)→ p4 可用:MTP → DSpark(置信度调度投机解码)
- scale-up 容量阶梯按 B300 288GB HBM 校正:~288GB → ~2.3TB(HGX 8 卡)→ ~20TB(NVL72),替代用户草案的 200G/2T/20T

## 交付物与目录结构

新建**独立工作区** `~/projects/aifactory-deck/`(与模拟器仓库完全分离,自成 git 仓库以便版本迭代;对 `~/projects/aifactory` 只读——截图/配色/公式口径按需**复制**进来并在 manifest 记录出处,不改模拟器任何文件):

```
aifactory-deck/
├── build.py                  # 读 content/ → 渲染 → out/aifactory-deck-v1.pptx
├── template/theme.py|master.py|layouts.py   # 配色/字体/母版/约6种版式渲染器
├── content/p01_*.py … p12_*.py + notes/*.md # 每页一个结构化 dict,长notes单独md
├── calc/capacity_model.py|financial_model.py|params.py|out/
├── assets/sim/|nvidia/|charts/|manifest.yaml # 截图/官网素材/生成图表+来源清单
├── check/render_pdf.sh|lint_deck.py
└── out/
```

- 模板:16:9,12 列网格;浅色商务风(白底,主色从 `src/lib/palette.ts` 提取一个品牌色 + 2 强调色 + SLA 语义色);中文 PingFang SC(theme 参数化,可切 Microsoft YaHei 重 build);每页五要素:页题/副题/内容区/页脚(页码)/右下来源角标(继承模拟器可溯源文化)
- 内容用 Python dict 而非 YAML:p2/p5/p5-x/p11-x 的数字直接 `import` calc/ 输出,杜绝手抄
- 图表策略:架构图/流程图/阶梯图用**原生 shapes**(写一个节点/分组/连线三原语的小 DSL,售前可现场改);数据图用 **matplotlib→PNG**(先读 dataviz skill);平台/网络/机房实景用**模拟器截图 + NVIDIA 官网素材**
- 依赖用 `uv` 装(python-pptx、matplotlib);渲染检查用 `/Applications/LibreOffice.app/Contents/MacOS/soffice --headless --convert-to pdf` + pdftoppm 逐页 PNG(soffice 不在 PATH 但 app 已装)

## 执行阶段

### 阶段 1:研究(并行 Agent fan-out)+ 模板开发
P0(阻塞 calc 出数,先行):
- A1 模型 KV 口径:从 HF config/tech report 抽 GLM-5.2/5.3、K3、V4×2 的层数/heads/latent/压缩比 → 产出 capacity_model 参数 dict

P2(骨架完成后补):A7 存储(VAST/WEKA/DDN 分层参考架构、模型加载带宽案例);A8 机房($/MW、DLC 改造周期、142kW 机柜要求);A9 运维与 PoC(AIOps agent 案例、MLPerf/GenAI-Perf/goodput 方法论);A10 行业 token 增速数据(OpenRouter、大厂财报)

同时:搭 template/ + build.py 骨架,先出 3 页样张(p1/p3/p6 各代表一种版式)供用户看视觉方向。

### 阶段 2:calc/ 两个模型
- `capacity_model.py`(移植 `src/lib/roofline.ts` 口径 + 混合注意力扩展):
  显存/worker = W(总参×bytes) + KV(并发×ctx×kv_bytes/token,分 GQA/MLA/KDA=0/CSA×压缩比四口径,K3 仅 24 层 MLA 计入) + OH(0.1W+2GB+常数注意力状态) × 安全系数 1.15–1.3 → GPU 数=ceil(需求÷HBM×0.9) → TP×EP 形态(scale-up 优先 8→72) → 单 worker 吞吐(优先公开 benchmark,无则 roofline 带宽近似,MBU 0.5/0.6/0.7 三档) → worker/节点/机架数(峰值余量 0.7)
  继承 roofline.ts 的 **null 纪律**:口径查不到就给区间/N/A + 假设标注,不伪造精确值
- `financial_model.py`(吃 capacity 输出的机架数):
  年收入 = Σ模型 [Q_out×P_out + Q_in×(h×P_cached+(1−h)×P_in)]×12,Q_out=C_tpm×U×60×24×30÷(1+R)
  年利润 = 收入 − CapEx/5 − 电费(142kW×PUE1.25×N_rack×8760×$0.07) − 托管 − 人力
  默认参数集中在 params.py:R=4:1、h=50%、U=40%、GB300 $4.5M;敏感性矩阵(单价 3.5/4.5/6.5M × 利用率 25/40/60%)。**初算利润可能为负——不回避,做成盈亏平衡条件叙事**(达到 X% 利用率/Y 价格才盈利),这体现售前专业度

- **p4** 推理服务逻辑架构:API GW → cache/load-aware Router → 多 model worker pool → prefill/decode 分离 → TP/PP/EP(DeepEP)+ 多级 KV(HBM→DRAM→NVMe);每环节挂影响指标标签(TTFT/TPOT/吞吐/成本);右栏技术点清单:continuous batching、chunked prefill、agg vs disagg、量化 FP8/FP4、MTP→DSpark、DCP、KV offload;**notes 重头**:每技术点收益/代价/适用/不适用场景
- **p5** 容量规划:显存构成堆叠条(权重/KV/开销/安全系数,旁注 K3 与 V4 新注意力口径)+ 容量推导链公式;下半 scale-up 阶梯图(1 GPU 288GB→HGX 8 卡 2.3TB TP→NVL72 20TB TP+EP→再 scale-out PP/EP),贴 hgx-board + gb300-rack 截图
- **p5-1/2/3** worked-example 三段式(输入表→计算过程→输出 worker 形态),数字全部由 capacity_model.py 生成;对标公开部署配置(vLLM recipe/NIM)
- **p6** 四平台对比表:RTX PRO(官网图)/HGX B300/GB300 NVL72/Vera Rubin(模拟器截图);行:核心参数(模拟器 keySpecs)/可跑模型/扩展方式/机房门槛/参考成本(区间+来源)/交付周期/性能口径
- **p7** 网络:NVIDIA 官方 scale-up/scale-out 拓扑图为主视觉 + 部件参数表(NVLink/NVSwitch/CX-8/IB X800/Spectrum-X leaf-spine)+ 「支撑场景→影响指标」列(EP all-to-all→TPOT、KV 迁移→TTFT);N-S/Storage/OOB 各一行带过
- **p8** 存储(设计提案):「数据生命周期泳道图」——横轴推理业务动线(模型分发→加载→运行时→归档→RAG 检索),四泳道(本地 NVMe/高性能共享/对象存储/DB+向量库),每泳道标职责/位置/关键参数/影响指标(模型冷启动→新模型上线承诺、RAG 检索时延→端到端 TTFT)
- **p9** 机房电力液冷:按 p6 四平台列硬门槛(GB300 142kW→必须 DLC、CDU 水温、承重、周期、$/MW)+ 冷却/电力平面截图 + 官网 CDU 图
- **p10** 运维:场景×角色矩阵(发布/扩缩容/故障定位/性能回归/安全审计/成本优化 × SRE/推理工程师/平台/安全/FinOps),标 L0-L4 自动化程度,**AI agent 可承担的格子高亮**,notes 给依据
- **p11** PoC 与验收:原生 shapes 流程图(需求对齐→workload 画像→环境→基准测试(定 SLA 找最大 goodput)→SLA 验证→故障演练→验收);常见坑框(只测峰值不看 goodput、prompt 分布失真、cache 命中虚高、烤机不足)
- **p11-1/2/3** PoC 实例:输入信息项(QPS、长度分布、cache 特征)→必测输出(吞吐-延迟曲线、P95 TTFT/TPOT、单位成本、恢复时间)→假设示例数据表,与 p5-x worker 形态一致形成「规划→验证」闭环
- **p12** 四象限:BOM 摘要(来自 calc)/TCO 五年条形/风险 Top5(交期、价格波动、模型迭代重规划、许可合规、SLA 违约)/路线图愿景收尾(2026 文本 token 工厂→2027 多模态→Agent 原生平台,「从卖 token 到卖结果」)

### 阶段 5:构建、检查、交付
1. `python build.py` 出 out/aifactory-deck-v1.pptx
2. `check/lint_deck.py`:每页 notes 非空、来源角标非空、字号≥12pt、文本不超版式预算
3. `check/render_pdf.sh`:soffice headless → PDF → 逐页 PNG,自查溢出错位(LibreOffice 中文渲染仅作 lint,最终视觉以 PowerPoint/Keynote 打开为准)
4. SendUserFile 交付 pptx + 逐页预览 PNG;列出所有「待用户拍板」参数清单(含 tpm 另一口径对照)

## 关键参考文件
- `src/lib/roofline.ts`、`src/lib/capacity.ts` — capacity_model.py 的口径与 null 纪律移植源
- `src/data/models.ts` — 模型参数 dict 的结构范式
- `src/data/hgx-b300.ts` 等 keySpecs — p5/p6 硬件参数唯一来源(模拟器数据可溯源)
- `src/lib/palette.ts` — 主题色提取
- `tests/e2e/factory.spec.ts` — 截图清单与深链补拍参考
- `sources/` 券商 PDF — GB300 成本交叉背书

## 风险与 Fallback(要点)
- GB300 无官方价 → 区间+中值+敏感性,明注第三方估算
- 稀疏注意力 KV 精确口径查不到 → null 纪律,给上下界+假设标注
- 利润可能为负 → 盈亏平衡叙事,不做单点结论
- LibreOffice 渲染偏差 → 只做溢出 lint;python-pptx 不嵌字体 → 字体名参数化
- p3/p4 手绘照片、RTX PRO 模拟器补全、H3 视频产能模型 → 均为已知的 v2 迭代项

## 验证
- 模拟器仓库零改动(`git -C ~/projects/aifactory status` 保持干净;deck 工作区独立 git 管理,按版本打 tag 迭代)
- calc 脚本带自检:公式量纲检查、与 roofline.ts 对同一输入(deepseek-v3)的输出交叉核对
- 最终 pptx 逐页渲染 PNG 人工/agent 过一遍 + 交付用户评审;评审意见回流迭代
```

```text
## Model Parameters and Architecture

GLM-5.2 is a 744-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language model from Zhipu AI (branded Z.ai) — released June 13, 2026 and now fully open source under the MIT license, with the complete weights live on Hugging Face.

GLM-5.2 uses roughly 750B parameters in a sparse MoE design, with around 40B active parameters per token, paired with a new "IndexShare" sparse-attention technique designed to keep 1M-context inference costs under control.

## Context Window and Capabilities

It marks a substantial leap in long-horizon task capability over its predecessor GLM-5.1 and, for the first time, delivers that capability on a solid 1M-token context. GLM-5.2's new capabilities include advanced coding with flexible effort levels and an improved architecture with IndexShare, which reuses the same indexer across every four sparse attention layers, reducing per-token FLOPs by 2.9× at a 1M context length.

## Open Source Availability

Zhipu AI has officially open-sourced GLM-5.2, putting the full weights of its 744-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model on Hugging Face under a permissive MIT license.
```

```text
Based on the search results, here's what I found about Kimi-K3 from Moonshot AI:

## Architecture Overview

Kimi-K3 is a 2.8T-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model built with Kimi Delta Attention, Attention Residuals, and Stable LatentMoE, with 104B activated parameters and a 1M-token context window.

## Key Architectural Components

**Attention Mechanisms:**
The model combines 69 KDA layers with 24 gated multi-head latent-attention layers. Every token flows through a 3:1 KDA-to-MLA cycle.

**Expert Configuration:**
The model contains 896 experts and selects 16 experts per token, with two shared experts. K3 pushes the pool to 896 but activates 16, more than recent frontier MoEs, landing at 1.8% active.

**Attention Residuals:**
AttnRes is the genuinely novel piece: instead of every block adding uniformly onto one residual stream, blocks selectively retrieve representations from earlier depths. Think of it as attention over depth, not just sequence.

## Additional Features

A 401M-parameter MoonViT-V2 vision encoder supports text and image understanding. The model supports a context length of 1,048,576 tokens.
```

```text
Based on the search results, here's what I found about DeepSeek-V4 Flash Pro sparse attention CSA parameters on Hugging Face:

## Hybrid Attention Architecture

DeepSeek-V4 uses a hybrid attention mechanism combining Compressed Sparse Attention (CSA) and Heavily Compressed Attention (HCA) to dramatically improve long-context efficiency.

## CSA Parameters

Compressed Sparse Attention (CSA) uses a low-compression pool with a default compression rate (m=4) with overlapping windows, plus a Lightning Indexer that scores queries against the pool and gathers the top index_topk blocks per query before they reach core attention.

More specifically, CSA compresses KV entries 4x along the sequence dimension using softmax-gated pooling with a learned positional bias. A lightning indexer (run in FP4, a ReLU-scored multi-head dot product) selects the top-k compressed blocks per query, and a sliding-window branch handles the most recent uncompressed tokens.

## Model Architecture Configuration

Per the HF blog, V4-Pro is a 61-layer stack where layers 0 and 1 are HCA and layers 2 through 60 alternate CSA and HCA.

## Performance Efficiency

In the 1M-token context setting, DeepSeek-V4-Pro requires only 27% of single-token inference FLOPs and 10% of KV cache compared with DeepSeek-V3.2.

The model weights and documentation are available on Hugging Face's official repository for both the V4-Flash and V4-Pro variants.
```

```text
## Release and Announcement

MiniMax announced H3 on July 31, 2026 and published its open-weight release on August 3.

## Parameters

MiniMax H3 is a 33-billion-parameter, omni-modal audio-video system.

## License

MiniMax H3 is released under the MiniMax H3 Community License Agreement. However, the license comes with significant territorial restrictions: the model's license requires users in the U.S., the UK, the European Union, and South Korea to submit an application to MiniMax to use it under the same terms as the rest of the world. The license also excludes open-weight use in the United States, European Union, United Kingdom, and South Korea unless MiniMax grants separate authorization.

## Model Architecture

The architecture is a Transformer with 33 billion parameters, separate text, audio, and video encoders, preprocessor, and 2K video upscaler. H3-Context-IR interprets free-form multimodal inputs and turns them into a structured intermediate representation. H3-Base generates audio-video at 768P. H3-Regenerate-2K uses the original context and a lower-resolution result to create a 2K version.

## Key Features

The official open-release specification is 4–15 seconds at 24 FPS, and it generates native 32 kHz stereo audio and lists stable dialogue support for 11 languages.
```

```text
Based on the web search results, here's information about vLLM recipes for DeepSeek-V4-Flash deployment with GPU tensor parallelism:

## vLLM Recipes for DeepSeek-V4-Flash

### Official vLLM Recipe

DeepSeek-V4-Flash is a 284B-total / 13B-active MoE model in the V4 preview family. It pairs a hybrid attention stack — Compressed Sparse Attention (CSA) + Heavily Compressed Attention (HCA) — with Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC) to reach 27% of V3.2's per-token inference FLOPs and 10% of V3.2's KV cache at 1M context.

### Tensor Parallel Deployment Configuration

For GPU tensor parallel deployment, the key flags are --tensor-parallel-size and --enable-expert-parallel, with --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla and --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 required for this model.

The Tensor + Expert Parallel strategy emits --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel for multi-GPU configurations.

### Practical Multi-Node Deployment Examples

For multi-node tensor parallel setups, the recipe serves DeepSeek-V4-Flash across 2x DGX Spark (GB10) with TP=2, achieving ~41 tokens/sec decode (single-stream) with 200K context.
```

```text
## Key Deployment Information

### Hardware Requirements

GLM-5.2 is a roughly 753B mixture-of-experts model with about 40B active parameters that requires around 744 GB of VRAM in FP8, which means an 8x H200 node in practice.

B200 serves the NVFP4 checkpoint at up to 500K context with HiCache CPU offload; H200 serves the FP8 checkpoint at up to 250K context.

### Quantization Options

SGLang's official GLM-5.2 recipe does not list an INT4 build. On Hopper, FP8 on 8x H200 is the single-node setup, though there is an NVFP4 checkpoint at roughly half the size that is Blackwell-only (B200 and up).

### SGLang Deployment

You can deploy GLM-5.2 with SGLang on H200, B200, B300, GB300, and AMD MI300X/MI325X/MI355X. SGLang's RadixAttention provides a long-context advantage — for a coding agent that re-uses 100K tokens of system prompt across every turn, you'll see approximately 3x the requests/second versus vLLM.

### Context Window Support

For the 1M-token context window, budget an additional 80-160 GB for KV cache beyond the weight footprint, making 8x H200 or 8x B200 the practical minimum for 1M-context workloads.

The official SGLang documentation provides a command generator tool where you can select your specific hardware and serving strategy to generate the appropriate launch commands for your deployment.
```

# Firecrawl CLI

Web scraping, search, and page interaction CLI. Returns clean markdown optimized for LLM context windows.

Run `firecrawl --help` or `firecrawl <command> --help` for full option details.

## Prerequisites

Must be installed and authenticated. Check with `firecrawl --status`.

```
  🔥 firecrawl cli v1.8.0

  ● Authenticated via FIRECRAWL_API_KEY
  Concurrency: 0/100 jobs (parallel scrape limit)
  Credits: 500,000 remaining
```

- **Concurrency**: Max parallel jobs. Run parallel operations up to this limit.
- **Credits**: Remaining API credits. Each scrape/crawl consumes credits.

If not ready, see [rules/install.md](rules/install.md). For output handling guidelines, see [rules/security.md](rules/security.md).

```bash
firecrawl search "query" --scrape --limit 3
```

## Workflow

Follow this escalation pattern:

1. **Search** - No specific URL yet. Find pages, answer questions, discover sources.
2. **Scrape** - Have a URL. Extract its content directly.
3. **Map + Scrape** - Large site or need a specific subpage. Use `map --search` to find the right URL, then scrape it.
4. **Crawl** - Need bulk content from an entire site section (e.g., all /docs/).
5. **Interact** - Scrape first, then interact with the page (pagination, modals, form submissions, multi-step navigation).

| Need                        | Command               | When                                                      |
| --------------------------- | --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Find pages on a topic       | `search`              | No specific URL yet                                       |
| Get a page's content        | `scrape`              | Have a URL, page is static or JS-rendered                 |
| Find URLs within a site     | `map`                 | Need to locate a specific subpage                         |
| Bulk extract a site section | `crawl`               | Need many pages (e.g., all /docs/)                        |
| AI-powered data extraction  | `agent`               | Need structured data from complex sites                   |
| Interact with a page        | `scrape` + `interact` | Content requires clicks, form fills, pagination, or login |
| Download a site to files    | `download`            | Save an entire site as local files                        |

For detailed command reference, run `firecrawl <command> --help`.

**Scrape vs interact:**

- Use `scrape` first. It handles static pages and JS-rendered SPAs.
- Use `scrape` + `interact` when you need to interact with a page, such as clicking buttons, filling out forms, navigating through a complex site, infinite scroll, or when scrape fails to grab all the content you need.
- Never use interact for web searches - use `search` instead.

**Avoid redundant fetches:**

- `search --scrape` already fetches full page content. Don't re-scrape those URLs.
- Check `.firecrawl/` for existing data before fetching again.

## Output & Organization

Unless the user specifies to return in context, write results to `.firecrawl/` with `-o`. Add `.firecrawl/` to `.gitignore`. Always quote URLs - shell interprets `?` and `&` as special characters.

```bash
firecrawl search "react hooks" -o .firecrawl/search-react-hooks.json --json
firecrawl scrape "<url>" -o .firecrawl/page.md
```

Naming conventions:

```
.firecrawl/search-{query}.json
.firecrawl/search-{query}-scraped.json
.firecrawl/{site}-{path}.md
```

Never read entire output files at once. Use `grep`, `head`, or incremental reads:

```bash
wc -l .firecrawl/file.md && head -50 .firecrawl/file.md
grep -n "keyword" .firecrawl/file.md
```

Single format outputs raw content. Multiple formats (e.g., `--format markdown,links`) output JSON.

## Working with Results

These patterns are useful when working with file-based output (`-o` flag) for complex tasks:

```bash
# Extract URLs from search
jq -r '.data.web[].url' .firecrawl/search.json

# Get titles and URLs
jq -r '.data.web[] | "\(.title): \(.url)"' .firecrawl/search.json
```

## Parallelization

Run independent operations in parallel. Check `firecrawl --status` for concurrency limit:

```bash
firecrawl scrape "<url-1>" -o .firecrawl/1.md &
firecrawl scrape "<url-2>" -o .firecrawl/2.md &
firecrawl scrape "<url-3>" -o .firecrawl/3.md &
wait
```

For interact, scrape multiple pages and interact with each independently using their scrape IDs.

## Credit Usage

```bash
firecrawl credit-usage
firecrawl credit-usage --json --pretty -o .firecrawl/credits.json
```

```text
# DeepSeek-V4-Flash Deployment Recipe

## Model Overview
DeepSeek-V4-Flash is a 284B-total/13B-active MoE model with "hybrid attention stack — Compressed Sparse Attention (CSA) + Heavily Compressed Attention (HCA)". It supports up to 1M context length.

## Recommended Hardware & Parallelism

**Multi-GPU Standard Setup:**
- Single-node DP + EP with `--data-parallel-size 4`
- Fills GB200 NVL4 tray; uses 4 of 8 GPUs on H200/B200/B300

**Variant-Specific Hardware:**
- **DGX Spark (GB10):** 2 nodes, TP2 (one GB10 per node)
- **DGX Station:** Single GPU with TP1
- **RTX PRO 6000:** 8× GPUs with TP8 + expert parallelism (sm_120 variant)
- **MI300X/MI325X/MI355X:** ROCm support with varying TP configurations

## Quantization & KV Cache
- **Default:** FP8 (0731 release) with "FP4+FP8 mixed" expert/other weight split
- **Alternative:** NVFP4 variant for Blackwell GPUs
- **KV Cache dtype:** `fp8` or `fp8_e4m3` (MI325X uses latter)

## Speculative Decoding Options

**DSpark (Recommended for 0731):**
```
--speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}'
```

**MTP (Preview variant):**
```
--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
```

## Key Launch Flags

**Essential parameters:**
- `--trust-remote-code`
- `--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4`
- `--tool-call-parser deepseek_v4`
- `--reasoning-parser deepseek_v4`
- `--enable-auto-tool-choice`

**Performance tuning:**
- `--block-size 256`
- `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9` (0.85 on MI300X)
- `--attention_config.use_fp4_indexer_cache True` (SM100 only; False for sm_120)

## Context & Output
- **Standard context:** 4K–1M tokens
- **Think Max reasoning:** Requires `--max-model-len >= 393216` (384K tokens)
- **Max output:** Up to 384K tokens at high/max reasoning levels

## Disaggregated Serving (H200 Example)
- Prefill: 4 GPUs with `--data-parallel-size 4`
- Decode: 4 GPUs with `--data-parallel-size 4`, `--max-num-seqs 512`
- KV transfer: MooncakeConnector (RDMA) or NixlConnector

## Benchmark Results
On MI355X (4×288GB), GSM8K evaluation achieved "0.9439" exact match with 8-shot configuration.
```

```text
# SGLang GLM-5.2 Deployment Recipe

## Supported Hardware
The documentation specifies deployment across several high-end accelerators: H200, B200, B300, GB300, and AMD MI300X/MI325X/MI355X variants.

## Key Configuration Parameters

**Quantization Options:**
- FP8 (primary focus in benchmarks)
- NVFP4 (newer precision format)
- BF16 (full precision alternative)

**Parallelism Settings:**
The system supports tensor parallelism (TP), expert parallelism (EP), and data parallelism (DP) configurations. The playground interface allows dynamic adjustment of these parameters, with automatic constraint validation.

**Context Window:**
The model supports "1M context" capability, representing extended sequence length handling.

## Deployment Strategies

Three execution profiles are offered:
- **Low-latency**: Optimized for minimal time-to-first-token (TTFT ~300-700ms range)
- **Balanced**: Mid-ground configuration (TTFT ~5-7s, handling 64-256 concurrent requests)
- **High-throughput**: Maximum token generation rate (1000+ concurrency scenarios)

## Speculative Decoding

The system includes "MTP speculative decoding" (Mixture-of-Tokens Parallel), with alternative algorithms like DSpark and N-gram available. The interface warns that speculative modes automatically reset `--max-running-requests` to 48 when unspecified.

## Sample Benchmarks (H200, FP8)

- Low-latency (bs=1): TTFT 668ms, TPOT 5.05ms, ~197 tokens/sec
- Balanced (bs=64): TTFT 7473ms, TPOT 23.49ms, ~2343 tokens/sec
- High-throughput (bs=1024): TPOT 61.71ms, ~1656 tokens/sec

B200 and GB300 show improved metrics (B200 balanced: 3078 tokens/sec at bs=64).

## Launch Pattern

Commands follow: `sglang serve --model-path [model] --tp [size] [quantization-flags] [parallelism-options] --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000`

Multi-node deployments inject `--nnodes`, `--node-rank`, and distributed initialization parameters automatically.
```

```text
# Benchmark Details Extraction

## Model & Hardware
- **Model:** DeepSeek-V4-Pro 1.6T (49B activated per token, MoE architecture)
- **Hardware Compared:** GB300 NVL72 vs GB200 NVL72 (both Blackwell generation)

## Key Hardware Differences
- GB300: 288GB HBM, 15 PFLOP/s FP4
- GB200: 192GB HBM, 10 PFLOP/s FP4
- Ratio: GB300 provides 1.5x HBM capacity and 1.5x FP4 compute
- TCO: GB300 costs 20% more ($2.65 vs $2.21/GPU/hr)

## Software Stack
- **Framework:** Dynamo + vLLM
- **Architecture:** Disaggregated prefill/decode across separate GPU pools
- **Quantization:** FP4
- **Context:** 8K input sequence length / 1K output sequence length

## Parallelism Configurations

**GB200 optimal recipes:**
- Prefill: 8-24 GPUs, TP=8
- Decode: 8-32 GPUs, EP=1 to EP=8

**GB300 optimal recipes:**
- Prefill: 4-28 GPUs, TP=4-8
- Decode: 8-68 GPUs, EP=1 to EP=16

## Throughput Results (Iso-Interactivity Comparison)

At 27 tok/s/user interactivity:
- GB200: 2,189 tok/s/GPU (~$0.28/M tokens)
- GB300: 6,182 tok/s/GPU (~$0.12/M tokens)
- **Throughput advantage:** 2.83x
- **Cost advantage:** 2.31x per million tokens

## Key Conclusion
The extra HBM capacity on GB300 "removes a software constraint" enabling wider prefill-decode batch configurations that GB200 cannot accommodate, delivering substantial efficiency gains despite identical memory bandwidth and fabric specifications.
```

```text
## Key Performance Comparison

Benchmarks show the NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell running on Akamai Cloud delivers up to 1.63x higher inference throughput than the H100. Another independent benchmark found that RTX PRO 6000 beats H100 SXM on single-GPU LLM inference at 28% lower cost per token.

## Memory and Architecture Differences

The RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell is a professional workstation and server GPU built on NVIDIA's newer Blackwell architecture, shipping with 96GB of GDDR7 ECC memory and is currently the only GPU under $10,000 capable of running 70B parameter language models on a single card without quantizing below Q4.

In contrast, the H100 is NVIDIA's previous-generation datacenter GPU, built on the Hopper architecture, with 80GB of HBM3 memory and memory bandwidth of up to 3.35 TB/s on the SXM variant.

## Multi-GPU Scaling

However, the advantage shifts at scale: H100 and H200 NVLink pull 3-4x ahead on 8-way tensor parallel. This is because the H100's NVLink interconnect provides significantly higher bandwidth for multi-GPU communication compared to the RTX PRO 6000's PCIe connections.

The results show that RTX PRO 6000 excels for single-GPU inference workloads with better cost efficiency, while H100/H200 systems with NVLink scale better for large distributed training and multi-GPU inference scenarios.
```

```text
Based on the web search results, here's comprehensive information about NVIDIA Dynamo's architecture components:

## Core Components

NVIDIA Dynamo's architecture integrates four core components: the Dynamo Planner for dynamic GPU allocation, the Smart Router for KV cache-aware request routing, the Distributed KV Cache Manager for offloading cache to cost-effective memory hierarchies, and the NVIDIA Inference Transfer Library (NIXL) for low-latency, hardware-agnostic data movement.

## Component Details

**Smart Router (KV-aware Router)**
For Large Language Models (LLMs), Dynamo employs KV cache-aware routing, which directs requests to the worker with the highest cache hit rate while maintaining load balance, expediting decoding. This routing strategy leverages a KV cache manager that maintains a global radix tree registry for hit rate calculation.

**Dynamo Planner (SLO Planner)**
A planning and scheduling engine that monitors capacity and prefill activity in multi-node deployments adjusting GPU resources to consistently meet Service Level Objectives (SLO).

**KV Block Manager (KVBM)**
The Dynamo KV Block Manager (KVBM) is a scalable runtime component designed to handle memory allocation, management, and remote sharing of Key-Value (KV) blocks for inference tasks across heterogeneous and distributed environments. The Dynamo KV Block Manager (KVBM) enables KV cache offloading to system CPU memory, local SSDs, and network-attached storage, allowing more KV blocks to be reused instead of recomputed.

**NIXL (Low-Latency Communication Library)**
NIXL is a low latency point-to-point inference data transfer library that accelerates the transfer of KV cache between GPUs and across heterogeneous memory and storage types. NIXL can abstract data movement across different types of memory and fast storage, whereas other data transfer libraries typically support a single tier of memory.

## Disaggregated Serving Support

NVIDIA Dynamo supports major LLM frameworks including NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, SGLang, and PyTorch, enabling developers to apply disaggregated serving optimizations without changing their inference backend.
```

```text
## Overview
NVIDIA AI Factory provides a full-stack reference architecture for deploying single-tenant AI solutions from infrastructure provisioning through agentic AI workloads, covering accelerated computing platforms, high-performance networking, Kubernetes-based deployment, observability, security, and partner integrations.

## Architecture Layers and Components

**Infrastructure Layer:**
The full Enterprise AI factory stack includes NVIDIA Blackwell for accelerated computing, BlueField for infrastructure acceleration, Spectrum-X networking for high-speed AI compute fabrics, and NVIDIA AI Enterprise software.

**Software Stack:**
The application layer includes AI frameworks, NIM microservices, and SDKs, while the Infrastructure Layer includes GPU drivers, Kubernetes operators, and cluster management tools.

## Reference Architecture Components

Each Enterprise RA includes recommendations for accelerated infrastructure based on optimized NVIDIA-Certified server configurations, featuring the latest NVIDIA GPUs, CPUs and networking technologies that have been tested and validated to deliver performance at scale.

## AI Factory Configurations

Three NVIDIA AI Factory configurations are available: the NVIDIA RTX PRO AI Factory (with NVIDIA RTX PRO Servers), NVIDIA HGX AI Factory (with NVIDIA HGX-based systems), and NVIDIA NVL72 AI Factory (with rack-scale systems based on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 platform).
```

```text
Based on the search results, here's what I found about SGLang's router and related features:

## SGLang Router with Cache-Aware Load Balancing

SGLang provides a router for deploying PD (Prefill-Decode) disaggregation at scale with load balancing and fault tolerance, which can distribute requests between prefill and decode instances using various routing policies.

The SGLang Router supports multiple load balancing policies including random, round-robin, cache-aware, and power-of-two selection.

## Prefill-Decode Disaggregation

The Prefill phase is computation-intensive, processing the entire input sequence, while the Decode phase is memory-intensive, managing the Key-Value (KV) cache for token generation. Traditionally, these phases are handled within a unified engine, where combined scheduling of prefill and decode batches introduces inefficiencies.

## HiCache and Hierarchical KV Cache

HiCache is SGLang's first-class in-tree offloading mechanism that offloads the full-attention cache and reconstructs the short sliding-window tail on the way back.

SGLang implements Incremental KV Transfer where Decode queries storage for cached prefix tokens and reports the hit count to Prefill via protocol extension; Prefill only transfers the non-cached (incremental) portion.

## Cache-Aware Routing and Affinity

SGLang implements DP-aware prefill and decode routing so both halves of a disaggregated deployment make that decision consistently, and adds cache balance as a routing signal so affinity does not degenerate into one hot worker.
```

```text
I found comprehensive information about vLLM's production-stack architecture with the features you're interested in. Here's what the search results reveal:

## Disaggregated Prefill/Decode Architecture

Prefill-decode (PD) disaggregation physically separates prefill and decode onto distinct GPU pools, with prefill nodes (P) processing incoming prompts and transferring the resulting KV cache to decode nodes (D) over the network, allowing D to perform autoregressive generation without interruption.

## KV Connector Components

In vLLM there are multiple connectors available for KV-cache transfer across GPUs. The Connector provides inter-instance connectivity, maintains the queue of requests awaiting remote prefill, and implements end-to-end KV-cache transfers between P-instances and D-instances, containing three primary components: (1) an instances metadata DB, (2) a prefill queue, and (3) a KV-cache transmitter.

AMD addresses this with MORI-IO, an RDMA-based KV cache connector contributed to vLLM, built on top of the open-source MORI (Modular RDMA Interface) framework.

## Prefix Caching

When multiple requests share the same beginning (prefix), vLLM stores the computed results for that common part and reuses them for new requests. The Router is integrated with prefix-caching logic and for each request computes the expected KV-cache hits on each D-instance, combining that information with per-instance load reported by the Resource Monitor.

## Architecture Benefits

The disaggregated architecture allows each phase to be optimized for its specific computational characteristics, with prefill clusters configured with high-memory, high-bandwidth setups that excel at large batch processing.
```

```text
## Gateway API Inference Extension Overview

Gateway API Inference Extension was created to address the gap in LLM traffic routing by building on the existing Gateway API, adding inference-specific routing capabilities while retaining the familiar model of Gateways and HTTPRoutes.

## Key Components

Inference Gateway (IGW) is a proxy/load-balancer which provides optimized routing and load balancing for serving Kubernetes self-hosted generative AI workloads, simplifying deployment, management, and observability of AI inference workloads.

Inference Scheduler is an extendable component that makes decisions about which endpoint is optimal (best cost/best performance) for an inference request based on metrics and capabilities from model serving.

## llm-d Integration

Inference Gateway has partnered with vLLM to accelerate LLM serving optimizations with llm-d! llm-d is an extensible architecture designed to schedule inference requests efficiently across model-serving pods, with a central component being the Inference Gateway, which builds on the Kubernetes-native Gateway API Inference Extension to enable scalable, flexible, and pluggable request scheduling.

## Performance Benefits

In benchmark tests, this smart routing delivered up to 3x improvements in time-to-first-token and doubled throughput under SLO constraints.
```

```text
# NVIDIA Dynamo Kimi-K3 Deployment Recipe

## Hardware Configuration

- GB200: 16 GPUs across 4 nodes (aggregated) or 32 GPUs across 8 nodes (disaggregated with 4 prefill + 4 decode)
- GB300: 16 GPUs in 2 replicas (aggregated) or 24 GPUs across 6 nodes (disaggregated with prefill/decode split)

## Backend & Engine

vLLM serves the model with "FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE backend" and prefix caching enabled.

## Parallelism Strategy

- **GB200 aggregated:** TP16 across all GPUs
- **GB200 disaggregated:** TP16 for both prefill and decode workers
- **GB300 aggregated:** TP8 per replica with KV-aware routing across replicas
- **GB300 disaggregated:** TP8 per replica

## Quantization

"MXFP4 experts + BF16 dense, FP8 KV" precision applied across all deployments.

## Disaggregation & KV Routing

Prefill/decode disaggregation uses KV-aware routing at the frontend. KV transfer occurs via "NIXL over RDMA (IB)" on GB200 and "NIXL over MNNVL" on GB300.

## Performance Metrics

The documentation does not provide throughput or latency numbers. Maximum context window across all configurations: **1,048,576 tokens**.

## Additional Features

Multimodal support enabled with data-parallel encoder sharding; tool calling and reasoning parser support included.
```

```text
## Official Announcement

NVIDIA announced the RTX PRO Servers at COMPUTEX, speeding the trillion-dollar IT infrastructure transition to enterprise AI factories with a new NVIDIA Enterprise AI Factory validated design for building data centers that deliver universal acceleration for AI, design, engineering and business applications.

The RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell is a universal data center GPU for powering AI factories and accelerating demanding enterprise AI workloads, from multimodal AI inference and physical AI to design, scientific computing, graphics and video applications. Designed for multi-GPU server deployments requiring passive cooling, the NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Server Edition balances performance and energy efficiency to power enterprise data center workloads—including inference, fine-tuning, distributed rendering, HPC, and virtual workstations.

## RTX PRO 6000 vs H100 for Inference

The positioning differs significantly:

- **RTX PRO 6000 advantages**: The PRO 6000 (Blackwell) delivers significantly higher training and inference throughput, better real-world LLM performance, and much greater power efficiency, making it ideal for mixed workloads. - **Memory capacity**: Capacity is comparable: 96GB (RTX PRO 6000) vs 80–94GB (H100). The RTX PRO 6000 holds as much or more model state per card.

Overall, RTX PRO 6000 delivers much better price-to-performance for most users. At a significantly lower cost, it provides strong AI training and inference performance, higher FP32 compute, larger VRAM, and excellent 3D rendering support, making it ideal for workstations and mixed workloads.
```

```text
# DeepSeek V4 Performance Evolution: Day 0 to Day 43

## Model & Hardware Platforms

The analysis tracked **DeepSeek V4 Pro 1.6T** across four primary platforms:
- **GB300 NVL72** (72-GPU NVLink domain)
- **Huawei Ascend 950DT**
- **AMD MI355X**
- **NVIDIA B200/B300**

## Day 0 Performance Snapshot

Initial throughput-interactivity curves revealed stark contrasts:

**NVIDIA CUDA**: vLLM and SGLang delivered functional support immediately. GB200 NVL72 disaggregated prefill achieved "up to 5x better results than for a B200 run using lower interactivity configs."

**AMD ROCm**: MI355X produced only "1-2 tokens per user per second," rendering it impractical for deployment despite technical functionality.

**Huawei CANN**: One of only two stacks providing Day 0 support, alongside NVIDIA CUDA.

## Architecture Optimizations Enabling Performance Gains

### Wide Expert Parallelism (WideEP)
The GB300's advantage stemmed from "Wide EP is the main lever for GB300's excellent performance." The May 20th GB300 update widened decode to EP=16 (versus initial EP=8), scaling prefill workers to four-twelve per decode worker.

### MegaMoE Implementation
DeepSeek's fused MoE kernel achieved theoretical "1.92x speedup over the naive kernel," through wave-based scheduling that interleaves dispatch, grouped GEMMs, activation, and combine operations across expert batches.

## Performance Timeline

**MI355X Transformation** (Day 0 → Day 26):
The AMD team delivered **100x+ improvement** by replacing PyTorch fallbacks with AITER, Triton, and TileLang kernels. Key milestones included FP4 MoE support and AITER mHC kernels enabling MI355X to exceed H200 performance at lower interactivity levels by late May.

**GB300 Dramatic Gains** (June 2 Update):
W4A4 MXFP4 MegaMoE implementation drove the largest improvement. Topology rewrites shifted from narrow EP=8 (16,384 max concurrency) to wide EP=16 (21,504 concurrency) without touching kernels or precision.

**B200 Efficiency Gains** (Day 0 → June 5):
Tokens per provisioned megawatt improved from approximately 300,000 to nearly 500,000 at 50 tok/s/user interactivity—representing pure software optimization with unchanged hardware power envelope.

## Cost-Performance Results

By June 6, 2026, GB300 NVL72 with MTP achieved **$0.156 per million output tokens** at 50 tok/s/user interactivity (8K input/1K output context), dominating all tested platforms.
```

```text
## Port Configuration
The NVIDIA Quantum-X800 InfiniBand switch provides 144 ports of 800 Gb/s connectivity per port. These 144 ports are distributed across 72 octal small form-factor pluggable (OSFP) cages.

The Q3400-RA has 115.2Tb/s throughput with 144 800Gb/s non-blocking ports.

The switch includes hardware-based In-Network Computing with SHARP v4, adaptive routing, telemetry-based congestion control, performance isolation capabilities, and a dedicated port supporting the Unified Fabric Manager (UFM). The Q3400-RA is a 4U switch that leverages 200Gb/s-per-lane serializer/deserializer (SerDes) technology. The Q3400 is air-cooled. There is a separate OSFP 400Gb/s InfiniBand in-band management port (UFM).

## Scalability
The switch's high radix supports a two-level fat-tree topology capable of connecting up-to 10,368 ConnectX-8 network interface cards (NICs) with minimal latency and optimal job locality.
```

```text
Based on the web search results, here's what I found about Fireworks AI's FireAttention architecture, engineering approach, and global deployment:

## FireAttention Architecture

FireAttention is Fireworks' proprietary family of custom CUDA kernels that form the computational foundation of the inference engine. Fireworks' inference stack is optimized end-to-end: kernel work where it matters (attention and related hot paths), plus the scheduler, memory management, batching policy, model packaging, and routing logic that determines real-world latency and cost.

FireAttention incorporates FlashAttention-family algorithms, paged attention (vLLM-style KV-cache management), speculative attention, grouped-query attention (GQA), and sliding-window attention.

## Performance & Multi-Layer Optimization

With FireAttention, Fireworks' proprietary inference engine, developers access frontier quality intelligence with up to 10× faster speed and throughput. With FireOptimizer, Fireworks' proprietary optimization layer, they determine the best deployment configuration from 84,000+ possible combinations across speculative decoders, quantization levels, hardware SKUs, kernel options, etc.

## Global Deployment & Scheduling

Fireworks Virtual Cloud scheduler automatically allocates inference resources based on workload needs—whether that's global locality, autoscaling, compliance, or disaster resilience. Paired with their 3D Optimizer, it ensures every deployment is tuned for the ideal balance of speed, quality, and cost. Fireworks runs across eight major clouds behind a Virtual Cloud abstraction spanning 18+ regions.

## Multi-Host Deployment

FireAttention has a mode when a model can be distributed across multiple hosts, which is beneficial for long generations.
```

```text
Based on the search results, here's a comprehensive overview of the provisioned throughput terminology and offerings across these platforms:

## Provisioned Throughput Terminology

**AWS Bedrock:** AWS Bedrock uses "Provisioned Throughput" for reserved capacity. Bedrock's provisioned throughput is model-agnostic within a provider family, giving you more flexibility.

**Azure AI Foundry:** Azure uses Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) for predictable load and Standard (pay-as-you-go) for bursty traffic. PTU quota is model-independent: one pool covers any supported model in a region and deployment type. And the throughput a PTU yields depends on the model's input-to-output ratio.

**Google Vertex AI:** Vertex sells Generative AI Scale Units (GSUs) with per-model burndown rates that normalize tokens, characters, and images into one throughput figure.

## Key Differences

Bedrock wins on cost and latency for steady serverless inference, Vertex wins on training speed and batch throughput thanks to TPU hardware, and Azure's economics depend entirely on how predictable your traffic is. PTUs guarantee latency but cost more if utilization stays under 70%, making them most cost-effective for sustained, predictable workloads.
```

```text
Based on the search results, I found comprehensive information about the continuous batching benchmark from Anyscale:

## Overview

Anyscale's benchmark demonstrated how continuous batching enables 23x throughput in LLM inference while reducing p50 latency.

## What is Continuous Batching?

Continuous batching is a system-level LLM serving optimization in which the batch size is determined per iteration rather than remaining constant throughout generation. Anyscale's 2023 benchmark popularized the term, and the technique is also called dynamic batching or batching with iteration-level scheduling.

## Benchmark Details

The benchmark ran on Meta's OPT-13B model on a single NVIDIA A100 with 40GB of RAM, and vLLM using continuous batching plus continuous-batching-specific memory optimizations reached up to 23x throughput over static batching. The same benchmark showed 8x over static batching on Ray Serve and Hugging Face text-generation-inference, and 4x with FasterTransformer's optimized implementation.

## Key Benefits

Continuous batching improves throughput by wasting fewer opportunities to schedule new requests, and improves latency by being capable of immediately injecting new requests into the compute stream. When a sequence finishes, it is evicted and a waiting request takes its slot on the next iteration, so the GPU never idles waiting for the slowest request.

The benchmark is available in a GitHub repository at https://github.com/anyscale/llm-continuous-batching-benchmarks.
```

```text
Based on the search results, I found comprehensive information about DistServe:

## DistServe: Disaggregating Prefill and Decoding for Goodput-optimized LLM Serving

DistServe improves the performance of large language models (LLMs) serving by disaggregating the prefill and decoding computation. 

### The Problem

Existing LLM serving systems colocate the two phases and batch the computation of prefill and decoding across all users and requests, which leads to strong prefill-decoding interferences and couples the resource allocation and parallelism plans for both phases. LLM applications often emphasize individual latency for each phase: time to first token (TTFT) for the prefill phase and time per output token (TPOT) of each request for the decoding phase, and in the presence of stringent latency requirements, existing systems have to prioritize one latency over the other, or over-provision compute resources to meet both.

### The Solution

DistServe assigns prefill and decoding computation to different GPUs, hence eliminating prefill-decoding interferences.

### Benchmark Results

The performance improvements are significant: DistServe can serve 7.4x more requests or 12.6x tighter SLO, compared to state-of-the-art systems, while staying within latency constraints for > 90% of requests across various popular LLMs, applications, and latency requirements.
```

```text
Based on the search results, here's what I found about Sarathi-Serve's chunked prefill and its performance improvements:

## Overview

Sarathi-Serve is a high throughput and low-latency LLM serving framework that addresses the throughput-latency tradeoff in LLM inference.

## Chunked Prefill Technology

Sarathi-Serve introduces chunked-prefills which splits a prefill request into near equal sized chunks and creates stall-free schedules that adds new requests in a batch without pausing ongoing decodes. Stall-free scheduling unlocks the opportunity to improve throughput with large batch sizes while minimizing the effect of batching on latency.

## Performance Improvements

The benchmark results show significant improvements:

- For Mistral-7B on single A100 GPUs, Sarathi-Serve achieves 2.6x higher serving capacity and up to 3.7x higher serving capacity for the Yi-34B model on two A100 GPUs as compared to vLLM
- When used with pipeline parallelism on Falcon-180B, Sarathi-Serve provides up to 5.6x gain in the end-to-end serving capacity
- Leveraging chunked-prefills results in a 1.48× increase in capacity under relaxed SLOs and 3.6× increase

## Key Benefits

Uniform batches in Sarathi-Serve ameliorate the imbalance between iterations resulting in minimal pipeline bubbles, which contributes to both improved throughput and reduced latency impact on concurrent decode operations.
```

```text
## Official NVIDIA Claims

NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra (GB300 NVL72) delivers up to 50x higher throughput per megawatt and up to 35x lower cost per token than NVIDIA Hopper for low-latency agentic workloads, through hardware–software codesign, according to SemiAnalysis.

## Reasoning Behind the 50x Metric

The GB300 NVL72 delivers a 10x boost in user responsiveness (TPS per user) and a 5x improvement in throughput (TPS per megawatt), which together translate into a 50x leap in overall AI factory output.

More specifically, this combines 10x better latency measured as tokens per second per user and 5x higher throughput per megawatt relative to Hopper platforms.

## Performance Gains Attribution

The gains are attributed to a combination of Blackwell Ultra silicon advances and ongoing software stack optimization across TensorRT-LLM, Dynamo, Mooncake and SGLang.

## Workload Focus

The findings focus on low-latency and long-context workloads such as AI coding agents and interactive assistants, which now account for roughly half of AI software programming queries.
```

```text
## Throughput Speedup

FP8 quantization with LLaMA-v2-7B achieves a notable 2.3x inference speedup compared to FP16 on an H100 when first token latency is constrained to under 500ms with batch size 16. Additionally, NVFP4 quantization delivers up to 2-3x token generation throughput speedup on models including Qwen 23B, DeepSeek-R1-0528, and Llama Nemotron Ultra.

For higher throughput scenarios, MR-MXFP4 provides around 15,000 tokens/sec for large batch workloads on a B200 GPU: a 2.2x increase over BF16 and a 1.3x increase over FP8.

## Accuracy Preservation

NVFP4 quantization preserves nearly all original accuracy while delivering the throughput speedup. For small batch inference, weight-only micro-rotated FP4 quantization shows approximately 20% lower latency than FP8.

## Deployment Support

NVIDIA TensorRT Model Optimizer supports formats including NVFP4, FP8, INT8, and INT4, and quantized models can be deployed with inference engines such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, and Dynamo. FP8 is recommended for H100 and H200 (Hopper architecture) with native FP8 support, while FP4 (NVFP4) is recommended for B200 and GB200 (Blackwell) which added FP4 hardware support.
```

```text
## Key Performance Benchmarks

SGLang achieves 52.3k input tokens per second and 22.3k output tokens per second per node for 2000-token input sequences using prefill-decode disaggregation and large-scale expert parallelism, with 12 nodes each with 8 H100 GPUs.

More recent results show even higher performance: On an NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 system, SGLang served the DeepSeek R1 models at 26k input and 13k output tokens per second per GPU for prefill and decode, respectively.

## DeepEP and Architecture

Large-Scale Expert Parallelism is implemented using communication libraries like DeepEP, which uses different dispatch modes for prefill (high throughput) and decode (low latency). By disaggregating, SGLang can leverage the optimal DeepEP mode for each phase, maximizing overall system efficiency.

## Performance Improvements

Compared to vanilla tensor parallelism using the same resources, this optimized strategy improves the output throughput by up to 5x. Additionally, Multiple Token Prediction unlocks up to 60% higher output throughput for DeepSeek V3 without any loss in generation quality.

This represents the first open-source implementation to nearly match the throughput reported in the official DeepSeek blog at large scale.
```

```text
## Key Findings

**Acceptance Rate and Speedup:**
The acceptance rate of the second token prediction ranges between 85% and 90% across various generation topics, and this high acceptance rate enables DeepSeek-V3 to achieve a 1.8 times TPS (Tokens Per Second) speedup.

**How It Works:**
DeepSeek-V3 predicts the next 2 tokens through the MTP technique, and combined with the framework of speculative decoding, it can significantly accelerate the decoding speed of the model.

**Technical Implementation:**
The DeepSeek report treats MTP primarily as an auxiliary training objective that can be repurposed for speculative decoding, which turns the auxiliary path into a proposer that drafts a short continuation, and the main model checks those candidate tokens in one forward pass.

**Performance Impact:**
Real world practice data demonstrates that an MTP module achieves an acceptance rate of 80% to 90% for predicting the second subsequent token, and by predicting multiple tokens per step, MTP increases the inference batch size, which is crucial for boosting computational intensity and hardware utilization.

This represents a significant advancement in inference efficiency, allowing DeepSeek models to maintain quality while substantially reducing generation time.
```

```text
Based on the search results, here's what I found about Decode Context Parallelism (DCP) and long-context inference throughput benchmarking:

## Overview

Decode Context Parallelism represents a fundamental rethinking of how GPUs are organized for long-context inference, putting every GPU to work by sharding the sequence during attention, then immediately reconfiguring those same GPUs to amortize FFN weight loading across the full pool.

## Key Benchmark Results

On an 8×B200 node serving Kimi K2.6, DCP reached 6,091 tok/s/GPU at concurrency 512 with 82% KV usage, versus a baseline TP ceiling of ~1,863 tok/s/GPU that maxes out memory at concurrency 64.

## Technical Approach

DCP addresses a fundamental bottleneck in long-context LLM inference by sharding the KV cache along the sequence dimension so each GPU stores only 1/N of every request's KV data, rather than partitioning by attention head.

## vLLM Implementation

Users can add decode context parallel to further shard the KV cache along the T dimension by adding -dcp <size> to the command line. With larger dcp size, the KV cache duplication is reduced, but the communication overhead increases.

## Workload Characteristics

The benchmark uses an agentic multi-turn workload of long inputs paired with short generations, with inputs centered around a median of ~67k tokens paired with short ~400-token outputs.
```

```text
## LMCache and Mooncake Integration

LMCache is a vendor-neutral KV cache management layer designed to optimize LLM inference by reducing TTFT and increasing throughput, especially for long-context workloads, supporting persistent, tiered KV cache offloading to various storage backends including CPU RAM, local disk, Redis, Valkey, Mooncake, and InfiniStore.

## TTFT Improvements - Multi-Turn Benchmarks

Several significant performance improvements have been documented:

- **MoE Model Performance**: LMCache MP mode reduces TTFT by approximately 13× on average (0.29s vs. 3.98s) and improves tail latency by over 10× at p99 (1.30s vs. 13.55s).

- **Agentic Workloads on AMD MI300X**: Under stress (32 users / 100k context / agentic traces), LMCache delivers 3.0× lower TTFT avg, 2.1× lower p95, 2.6× lower max, 2.3× more requests vs HBM-only.

- **Mooncake Store with vLLM**: The distributed KV cache pool improves throughput by 3.8x, reduces P50 TTFT by 46x, and reduces E2E latency by 8.6x, driven by a cache hit rate increase from 1.7% to 92.2%.

- **SGLang HiCache**: HiCache achieved up to 6× throughput improvement and up to 80% reduction in TTFT.

## Multi-Turn Conversation Context

Offloading allows the model to skip redundant KV computations during inference, especially for overlapping context in multi-turn interactions, significantly reducing TTFT and overall latency.
```

```text
# SGLang GLM-5.3 Deployment Guide

## Supported Hardware & Configurations

GLM-5.3 deploys on **H200, B200, B300, GB300, and AMD MI300X/MI325X/MI355X** GPUs via SGLang, leveraging DeepSeek's sparse-attention mixture-of-experts architecture with up to **1M context**.

## Key Deployment Parameters

**Quantization & Precision:**
- FP8 quantization is the primary verified configuration
- Supports context lengths of 8,192 input / 1,024 output tokens in benchmarks

**Parallelism Strategy:**
- Tensor Parallelism (TP) configurable per hardware
- Expert Parallelism (EP) available for MoE workloads
- Data Parallelism (DP) with optional attention distribution (DP-Attention)

**Speculative Decoding:**
The system integrates MTP (Multi-Token Prediction) with EAGLE draft models:
- EAGLE 5/1/6 configuration for low-latency scenarios
- EAGLE 1/1/2 for high-throughput deployments

## Representative Benchmarks

| Hardware | Strategy | TTFT (ms) | TPOT (ms) | Throughput |
|----------|----------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| B200 | Low-latency (bs=1) | 400 | 3.11 | 321 tok/s |
| B200 | High-throughput (bs=256) | 18,916 | 31.88 | 5,025 tok/s |
| GB300 | Low-latency (bs=1) | 372 | 3.68 | 556 tok/s |
| GB300 | High-throughput (bs=256) | 25,775 | 45.87 | 7,501 tok/s |

**Accuracy metrics** (GSM8K): 97–97.7% across configurations; AIME2025: 90.6–92% in throughput modes.

All benchmarks use pinned accept lengths to isolate throughput behavior, not correctness validation.
```

```text
## DeepSeek-V4-Pro on GB200 NVL72

DeepSeek-V4-Pro recipes are available on Dynamo across vLLM and SGLang backends for GB200 hardware targets.

### Hardware Configuration

On GB200, the model exceeds a single 4-GPU NVL4 tray, so V4-Pro spans two GB200 trays via NVLink72 (MNNVL) — either aggregated with TP=8 cross-node or disaggregated prefill/decode.

### Deployment Approaches

For GB200 NVL4 (4× GPU per tray), the ~960 GB mixed-precision checkpoint does not fit on one tray; run multi-node DP + EP across 2 trays (8 GPUs total) with --data-parallel-size 8.

### Wide Expert Parallelism (WideEP)

Wide expert parallelism (WideEP) is an inference optimization technique that can considerably improve performance per dollar. vLLM and Nvidia delivered a GB200 distributed inference Dynamo vLLM recipe that supports this approach.

For more detailed deployment configurations and setup instructions, you can visit the official vLLM recipes page at https://recipes.vllm.ai/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro.
```

```text
## Key Specifications

**Network Performance:**
- Support for both InfiniBand and Ethernet networking at up to 800 gigabits per second (Gb/s)
- 800 Gb/s Infiniband XDR or 2x400G Ethernet Integrated Spectrum-X Ethernet interface with up to 8 ports

**PCIe Interface:**
- Integrates native PCIe Gen6 support with an on-board PCIe switching fabric
- PCIe Gen6 with 48 lanes, offered through an integrated PCIe switch
- The SuperNIC's 32-lane PCIe bus is split into two 16-lane buses, with one bus accessible through a PCIe x16 edge connector and the other bus through an x16 Auxiliary PCIe Connection card

**Product Models:**
- The C8180 is NVIDIA's first 800Gb/s dual-protocol SuperNIC for InfiniBand/Ethernet, belonging to the ConnectX-8 series
- The C8180 commonly comes in two models: 900-9X81E-00EX-ST0 supporting SocketDirect/Multi-Host, and 900-9X81E-00EX-DT0 supporting Downstream Port (DSP)

**Use Cases:**
- Primarily designed for AI high-performance computing clusters, supercomputing networks, and next-generation data center architectures
```

```text
## NVIDIA HGX B300 Specifications

**GPU Configuration:**
The NVIDIA HGX B300 is an eight-GPU accelerated computing platform built around Blackwell Ultra SXM GPUs, combining 2,304 GB of HBM3e memory, fifth-generation NVLink and NVSwitch connectivity, and eight ConnectX-8 SuperNICs.

**NVLink Bandwidth:**
NVIDIA specifies 1,800 GB/s of GPU-to-GPU NVLink bandwidth and 14.4 TB/s of total aggregate NVLink bandwidth for the platform.

**NVSwitch Configuration:**
The eight B300 GPUs form a scale-up domain through fifth-generation NVLink and two NVSwitch chips, with each GPU connecting to both NVSwitches on HGX B300 baseboards, providing all-to-all GPU communication within the node.

**Memory:**
Each GPU carries 270 GB of HBM3e memory.

**Networking:**
HGX B300 is externally connected by a network interface of 800 Gb/s (2 x 400Gb/s Ethernet) per GPU, provided by 8x ConnectX-8 SuperNICs on the HGX baseboard.
```

```text
Based on the search results, here's what I found about NVIDIA's BlueField DPUs and their role in storage and network infrastructure:

## BlueField-3 and BlueField-4 Specifications

The NVIDIA BlueField-3 DPU is a 400Gb/s infrastructure compute platform with line-rate processing of software-defined networking, storage, and cybersecurity. The NVIDIA BlueField-4 is an 800Gb/s infrastructure platform for gigascale AI factories.

## Network Traffic Roles

Most deployments will run using Ethernet at the front end, handling north-south traffic – the data flows between servers and storage systems, internet access for inference workloads, and the security services running directly on the BlueField-4 itself. For GPU-to-GPU communications – the "east-west" traffic that powers training and large-scale inference – Nvidia is packaging multiple ConnectX-9 chips together.

## Performance Improvements

The new generation moves data from storage to compute at rates of 800 Gbps, double the previous generation, with a 6x boost in computational power. A DPU paired with a network interface card (NIC) serves as a dedicated data mover, thereby unburdening the CPU from data movement overhead and allowing the cluster to get more useful work done.
```

```text
I found comprehensive information about NVIDIA's rail-optimized topology with leaf-spine GPU cluster reference architecture. Here are the key findings:

## Rail-Optimized Architecture Overview

Rail-optimized topology emerged from recognition that GPU servers contain multiple GPUs sharing high-speed internal interconnects. Rail-optimized design means a GPU node with multiple interfaces will put each GPU "rail" (IB network interface) onto a different first level (LEAF) switch for cluster Interconnect, allowing multiple nodes to utilize their internal NVSwitch path to talk across a NIC that is just one switch hop away.

## Leaf-Spine Fat Tree Topology

The leaf and spine architecture allows for a scalable and reliable network that can fit varied sizes of clusters using the same architecture. The compute fabric is built using switches with NVIDIA Spectrum technology in a full non-blocking fat tree topology.

## Two-Tier Fat Tree Configuration

A 16-node cluster requires two leaf switches with uplinks to one or two spine switches for inter-leaf communication, and a non-blocking two-tier fat-tree provides full bisection bandwidth across all GPUs. At 64 nodes, a two-tier fat-tree runs out of non-blocking port capacity, requiring a three-tier fat-tree topology instead.

## Specific GPU Implementation

NVIDIA's recommended topology for large AI training clusters is "rail-optimized": each of the 8 GPUs in a server connects to a different leaf switch. GPUs are connected using a rail-optimized network topology through their respective ConnectX-8 NICs.
```

```text
## Lead Time

Most organizations face a 6-12 month lead time to procure and deploy GB300 NVL72 systems. However, buyers ordering a DGX B300 in mid-to-late 2026 should budget for a realistic delivery window of two to five months, with the shorter end of that range applying to smaller orders through well-stocked partners and the longer end applying to larger custom configurations or partners further down NVIDIA's allocation queue.

## Production and Availability

GB300 systems entered production in Q3 2025 with Quanta shipping units starting September. As of early 2026, NVIDIA has begun the transition to the GB300 NVL72 (Blackwell Ultra) platform, announced at GTC 2025 and ramping through the first half of 2026.

## Allocation Challenges

GB200 NVL72 has been shipping over a year longer, is available across more providers, and if your timeline is measured in weeks rather than quarters, that is a real advantage. This suggests that GB300 availability remains more constrained than its predecessor.
```

```text
# NVL72 AI Factory Network Fabrics

## Compute/East-West Fabric
The compute fabric uses "switches with NVIDIA Spectrum technology in a full non-blocking fat tree topology" organized in a leaf-spine architecture. Each GPU connects via ConnectX-8 SuperNICs delivering 800 Gb/s of bandwidth.

**Dual Plane Design**: The architecture splits each GPU's 800 Gb/s into two 400 Gb/s interfaces, each connected to separate leaf switches. Each independent fabric can scale to 1024 interfaces of 400 Gb/s. This dual-plane approach provides redundancy and load balancing via NCCL hardware-level tracking.

The compute fabric supports models exceeding 1920B parameters through model parallelism across multiple trays via NVLink and NVSwitch technology.

## CPU Converged (North/South) Network
This Ethernet-based fabric carries storage and in-band management traffic independently from compute. Each tray connects using dual 400 Gb/s ports to two separate switches, enabling per-node storage bandwidth of up to 40 GB/s. The design incorporates "NVIDIA BlueField-3 B3240 DPUs in each compute tray" supporting RoCE (RDMA over Converged Ethernet).

## Out-of-Band Management Network
The OOB network connects base management controller ports and infrastructure devices at 1 Gb/s, remaining physically isolated from system users.
```

```text
I found comprehensive search results on this topic. Here's what the results reveal about expert parallelism, all-to-all communication, and the various interconnect technologies:

## NVLink vs InfiniBand Bandwidth

Moving from NVLink to InfiniBand dramatically increases communication overhead for all-to-all operations, with measurements showing a single all-to-all communication task taking 151.8 µs on lower-bandwidth fabric compared to 17.65 µs on high-bandwidth fabric for per-accelerator batch size of 128.

ConnectX 7 InfiniBand operates at 400 Gb/s per GPU, roughly 36x below NVL72's NVLink bandwidth. More specifically, InfiniBand/RoCEv2 Ethernet typically provides 400-800 Gbit/s per GPU uni-directional (50-100 GB/s).

## Expert Parallelism on NVL72

All 72 B200 GPUs on NVL72 sit on one flat NVSwitch fabric at 130 TB/s, where all-to-all communication at 72-GPU scale costs the same as at 8-GPU scale per byte transferred.

On NVL72, MoE traffic stays on NVLink 5 at 1.8 TB/s per GPU inside a 130 TB/s aggregate fabric.

## MoE Inference & Decode Performance

NVL72's rack-scale NVLink fabric lets decode run with wide expert parallelism up to Decode EP 16, with the peak at Decode EP 8 on an 8 GPU decode pool. B200 tops out at Decode EP 4 on the best measured recipe, after which the expert all-to-all starts hitting scale-out fabric latencies.

## All-to-All Dispatch/Combine in MoE

The all-to-all communication pattern, required to dispatch every token to its designated experts and then combine the results, creates dense network traffic that can easily become a bottleneck.

Recent optimization work (UBEP) reduces All-to-All latency by up to 52.4% and MoE inference Time Per Output Token (TPOT) by up to 11.1%.
```

```text
- Data-Parallel Attention: `--enable-dp-attention`
- Prefill Context Parallelism (CP): `--enable-prefill-cp`, `--attn-cp-size`

- W4A8 (MegaMoE default)
```

```text
Based on the web search results, here's a comprehensive summary of the key topics from your query:

## Prefill-Decode Disaggregation and KV Cache Transfer

Disaggregated serving runs prefill and decode on dedicated GPU node pools, transferring the KV between instances when a request transitions from prefill to decode. For disaggregated serving, KV cache transfer is on the critical path, and TTFT includes processing on prefill node, KV cache transfer and the return of the first token from the decode node.

## NIXL and Dynamo

NIXL (NVIDIA Inference Transfer Library) is an open-source library that handles GPU-to-GPU and GPU-to-NVMe KV cache transfers for disaggregated LLM inference. Dynamo uses NIXL to move that state directly between workers, choosing the best available transport such as NVLink or InfiniBand/UCX.

## InfiniBand and Network Bandwidth

NIXL supports libfabric as the backend for AWS EFA deployments, achieving ~9.6 GB/s KV transfer bandwidth. Additionally, transferring KV data from prefill GPUs to decoding GPUs demands immense network bandwidth—often requiring 90 Gbps or more just to render the transmission overhead invisible to the user.

For InfiniBand specifically, evaluations test three NIXL transport backends across three network transports: 100G RoCE, 400G NVIDIA Quantum-2 InfiniBand fabric, and 100G TCP.

## Per-Token Transfer Costs

The search results indicate that KV cache transfer latency and bandwidth requirements scale with context length and token counts, though specific per-token bandwidth metrics in GB/s were not explicitly stated in the available sources. The KV cache produced during prefill must be made available to decode, and in long-context serving, that cache is large enough for transfer bandwidth and transfer latency to become first-order concerns.
```

```text
# DSpark Paper Summary

**Title:** "DSpark: Confidence-Scheduled Speculative Decoding with Semi-Autoregressive Generation"

**Technique:** DSpark combines a semi-autoregressive architecture with confidence-scheduled verification. It pairs a "parallel backbone with a lightweight sequential module" to model dependencies and prevent performance decay, then dynamically adjusts verification length based on predicted token survival rates.

**Reported Benefits:**
- 60-85% acceleration in per-user generation speeds at matched throughput levels
- Substantial improvements in accepted token length over existing approaches
- Enables previously unattainable performance tiers by shifting the Pareto frontier

**Costs/Tradeoffs:** The paper mentions that parallel drafters "suffer from rapid acceptance decay" and indiscriminately verifying extended blocks "wastes critical batch capacity," which DSpark addresses through adaptive verification—though this requires overhead for confidence estimation.

**Target Scenario:** Speculative decoding for LLM inference, specifically addressing high-concurrency serving systems. The work references deployment within "the DeepSeek-V4 serving system under live user traffic" and comparison against "MTP-1" production baseline.
```

```text
AIBrix is a cloud-native, open-source framework designed to optimize and simplify large-scale LLM deployment in cloud environments. Serving as the control plane for vLLM, AIBrix ensures enterprise-grade reliability, scalability, and cost-effectiveness.

## Key Architecture Components
```

```python
BAD = 'D92D20'


def mix(a: str, b: str, t: float) -> str:
    """两个 RRGGBB 线性插值,t=0 取 a。用于生成浅色 tint。"""
    pa = [int(a[i:i + 2], 16) for i in (0, 2, 4)]
    pb = [int(b[i:i + 2], 16) for i in (0, 2, 4)]
    k = min(max(t, 0.0), 1.0)
    return ''.join(f'{round(va + (vb - va) * k):02x}' for va, vb in zip(pa, pb)).upper()


def tint(c: str, t: float = 0.9) -> str:
    """向白色靠拢的浅底色(t 越大越浅)。"""
    return mix(c, 'FFFFFF', t)
```

```text
# NVIDIA Dynamo Architecture Components

## Official Components and Responsibilities

**API Server**: Adapts to task-specific deployments and handles incoming user requests at the system entry point.

**Smart Router**: "Processes user requests to route them to the optimal worker for performance." For LLMs specifically, it employs KV cache-aware routing that directs requests to workers with the highest cache hit rate while maintaining load balance.

**Planner**: Makes "intelligent, zero-downtime adjustments" by responding to real-time deployment signals communicated through an event plane. Automatically scales workers based on demand patterns (e.g., scaling up prefill workers for long input sequences).

**KV Cache Block Manager (KVBM)**: Maintains a global radix tree registry for cache hit calculations and oversees "a multi-tiered memory system, enabling rapid KV cache storage and eviction" across GPU, CPU, SSD, and remote storage.

**Disaggregated Prefill & Decode Workers**: Separate compute stages—prefill handles embedding generation; decode handles token generation—optimizing throughput and latency independently.

**NIXL (NVIDIA Inference tranXfer Library)**: A data transfer engine designed to "expedite transfers through reduced synchronization and intelligent batching," abstracting movement across different memory tiers.

## Request Flow Layering

The architecture employs layered processing: User requests enter through the API Server, are routed via the Smart Router to appropriate workers, while the Planner orchestrates dynamic scaling and the KVBM manages distributed memory state across the system.
```
</details></tool-use>

# firecrawl scrape

Scrape one or more URLs. Returns clean, LLM-optimized markdown. Multiple URLs are scraped concurrently.

## When to use

- You have a specific URL and want its content
- The page is static or JS-rendered (SPA)
- Step 2 in the [workflow escalation pattern](firecrawl-cli): search → **scrape** → map → crawl → interact

## Quick start

```bash
# Basic markdown extraction
firecrawl scrape "<url>" -o .firecrawl/page.md

# Main content only, no nav/footer
firecrawl scrape "<url>" --only-main-content -o .firecrawl/page.md

# Wait for JS to render, then scrape
firecrawl scrape "<url>" --wait-for 3000 -o .firecrawl/page.md

# Multiple URLs (each saved to .firecrawl/)
firecrawl scrape https://example.com https://example.com/blog https://example.com/docs

# Get markdown and links together
firecrawl scrape "<url>" --format markdown,links -o .firecrawl/page.json

# Ask a question about the page
firecrawl scrape "https://example.com/pricing" --query "What is the enterprise plan price?"
```

## Options

| Option                   | Description                                                      |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-f, --format <formats>` | Output formats: markdown, html, rawHtml, links, screenshot, json |
| `-Q, --query <prompt>`   | Ask a question about the page content (5 credits)                |
| `-H`                     | Include HTTP headers in output                                   |
| `--only-main-content`    | Strip nav, footer, sidebar — main content only                   |
| `--wait-for <ms>`        | Wait for JS rendering before scraping                            |
| `--include-tags <tags>`  | Only include these HTML tags                                     |
| `--exclude-tags <tags>`  | Exclude these HTML tags                                          |
| `-o, --output <path>`    | Output file path                                                 |

## Tips

- **Prefer plain scrape over `--query`.** Scrape to a file, then use `grep`, `head`, or read the markdown directly — you can search and reason over the full content yourself. Use `--query` only when you want a single targeted answer without saving the page (costs 5 extra credits).
- **Try scrape before interact.** Scrape handles static pages and JS-rendered SPAs. Only escalate to `interact` when you need interaction (clicks, form fills, pagination).
- Multiple URLs are scraped concurrently — check `firecrawl --status` for your concurrency limit.
- Single format outputs raw content. Multiple formats (e.g., `--format markdown,links`) output JSON.
- Always quote URLs — shell interprets `?` and `&` as special characters.
- Naming convention: `.firecrawl/{site}-{path}.md`

## See also

- [firecrawl-search](../firecrawl-search/SKILL.md) — find pages when you don't have a URL
