13	 * **绝不允许把 null 当 0**——把未知 KV 当 0 会让长上下文吞吐虚高数倍。
14	 * 参考实现 llms-study/src/lib/simEngine.ts 的 `estStepMs` 在 KV 为 null 时按 0 计算，
15	 * 是一个已确认的 bug，本移植版已修正为返回 null。
16	 */
17	import type { KVSpec } from '../data/types'
18	
19	export interface QuantOption {
20	  id: 'fp16' | 'fp8' | 'int4'
21	  label: string
22	  bytesPerParam: number
23	}
24	
25	export const QUANTS: QuantOption[] = [
26	  { id: 'fp16', label: 'FP16/BF16', bytesPerParam: 2 },
27	  { id: 'fp8', label: 'FP8', bytesPerParam: 1 },
28	  { id: 'int4', label: 'INT4/FP4', bytesPerParam: 0.5 },
29	]
30	
31	export const DEFAULT_MFU = 0.4 // prefill 算力利用率（经验值）
32	export const DEFAULT_MBU = 0.6 // decode 带宽利用率（经验值）
33	
34	const KV_BYTES = 2 // KV 按 FP16 存储
35	
36	/** 权重显存：参数量(B) × 每参数字节 = GB（1e9 × bytes ÷ 1e9）。 */
37	export function weightMemoryGB(totalParamsB: number, bytesPerParam: number): number {
38	  return totalParamsB * bytesPerParam
39	}
40	
41	/**
42	 * 每 token 全层合计的 KV 字节数。
43	 * 新型稀疏/线性注意力无公开参数时返回 null（不做伪精确估算）。
44	 */
45	export function kvBytesPerToken(kv: KVSpec): number | null {
46	  switch (kv.kind) {
47	    case 'mha-gqa':
48	      return 2 * kv.kvHeads * kv.headDim * kv.numLayers * KV_BYTES
49	    case 'mla':
50	      // MLA 只缓存压缩后的 latent（如 DeepSeek 512+64=576 维），没有 K/V 两份
51	      return kv.kvLatentDim * kv.numLayers * KV_BYTES
52	    case 'unsupported':
53	      return null
54	  }
55	}
56	
57	export function kvCacheGB(kv: KVSpec, contextTokens: number, batch: number): number | null {
58	  const per = kvBytesPerToken(kv)
59	  if (per === null) return null
60	  return (per * contextTokens * batch) / 1e9
61	}
62	
63	export interface MemoryBreakdown {
64	  weightsGB: number
65	  kvGB: number | null
66	  overheadGB: number
67	  totalGB: number | null
68	}
69	
70	/** 开销：激活/运行时/碎片，简化为权重的 10% + 2GB。 */
71	export function memoryBreakdown(
72	  totalParamsB: number,
73	  bytesPerParam: number,
74	  kv: KVSpec,
75	  contextTokens: number,
76	  batch: number,
77	): MemoryBreakdown {
78	  const weightsGB = weightMemoryGB(totalParamsB, bytesPerParam)
79	  const kvGB = kvCacheGB(kv, contextTokens, batch)
80	  const overheadGB = weightsGB * 0.1 + 2
81	  return {
82	    weightsGB,
83	    kvGB,
84	    overheadGB,
85	    totalGB: kvGB === null ? null : weightsGB + kvGB + overheadGB,
86	  }
87	}
88	
89	/** 最少 GPU 数（默认只按 90% 显存可用，留服务余量）。 */
90	export function minGpus(totalGB: number, gpuMemoryGB: number, usable = 0.9): number {
91	  return Math.max(1, Math.ceil(totalGB / (gpuMemoryGB * usable)))
92	}
93	
94	/**
95	 * 按所选量化取 GPU 算力口径：仅在官方公布了对应精度算力时切换（INT4/FP4 → fp4Tflops），
96	 * 其余（含 FP16——数据层没有官方 FP16 字段）回退 FP8 口径，`basis` 供 UI 标注「按 FP8 算力口径」。
97	 * 不编造硬件数字：GPU 两个字段都为 null 时原样透传 null。
98	 */
99	export function tflopsForQuant(
100	  gpu: { fp8Tflops: number | null; fp4Tflops: number | null },
101	  quantId: QuantOption['id'],
102	): { tflops: number | null; basis: 'fp8' | 'fp4' } {
103	  if (quantId === 'int4' && gpu.fp4Tflops !== null) return { tflops: gpu.fp4Tflops, basis: 'fp4' }
104	  return { tflops: gpu.fp8Tflops, basis: 'fp8' }
105	}
106	
107	/** TTFT 估算（ms）：prefill FLOPs ≈ 2 × 激活参数 × prompt tokens。算力未知 → null。 */
108	export function estTTFTms(
109	  activeParamsB: number,
110	  promptTokens: number,
111	  gpuTflops: number | null,
112	  gpuCount: number,
113	  mfu = DEFAULT_MFU,
114	): number | null {
115	  if (gpuTflops === null) return null
116	  const flops = 2 * activeParamsB * 1e9 * promptTokens
117	  return (flops / (gpuTflops * 1e12 * gpuCount * mfu)) * 1000
118	}
119	
120	/**
121	 * 每个 decode 步的时长（ms）：读一遍激活权重（batch 内共享）+ batch 份 KV。
122	 *
123	 * ★ null 语义（与参考实现的关键差异）：`kvPerTokenBytes === null` 时**一律返回 null**，
124	 *   即使 `contextTokens === 0` 也返回 null。理由是语义统一——「KV 口径未知 ⇒ 不估算」，
125	 *   而不是「这次恰好算得出所以给个数」。调用方拿到 null 应显示 N/A 并说明缺失哪项官方数据。
126	 */
127	export function estStepMs(
128	  activeParamsB: number,
129	  bytesPerParam: number,
130	  kvPerTokenBytes: number | null,
131	  contextTokens: number,
132	  batch: number,
133	  bandwidthTBs: number,
134	  gpuCount: number,
135	  mbu = DEFAULT_MBU,
136	): number | null {
137	  if (kvPerTokenBytes === null) return null
138	  const weightBytes = activeParamsB * 1e9 * bytesPerParam
139	  const kvBytes = kvPerTokenBytes * contextTokens * batch
140	  return ((weightBytes + kvBytes) / (bandwidthTBs * 1e12 * gpuCount * mbu)) * 1000
141	}
142	
143	/** 集群总吞吐 tokens/s：每步产出 batch 个 token。步长未知 → null。 */
144	export function tokensPerSecond(stepMs: number | null, batch: number): number | null {
145	  if (stepMs === null) return null
146	  return (batch / stepMs) * 1000
147	}
148

# A6 — Scale-up / Scale-out 网络(NVIDIA 口径)

核实日期:2026-09-03。口径:2025–2026 官方页面 / 官方文档 / 官方博客为主,第三方仅作旁证。
适用 slide:「Scale-up/Scale-out 网络」页(含四张网总览)。

---

## 1. 部件参数表

| 部件 | 代际 | 关键带宽/容量 | 所属网络 | 来源 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NVLink 5 | Blackwell / Blackwell Ultra(GB200/GB300/HGX B300) | **1.8 TB/s per GPU**(18 links,900 GB/s 单向);GB300 NVL72 域聚合 **130 TB/s**(72 GPU + 36 Grace 单一 NVLink 域) | Scale-up | [1][2][5] |
| NVLink Switch(第 5 代 NVSwitch) | Blackwell | 每 switch tray **144 个 NVLink 端口 @100 GB/s**(每 tray 2 颗 NVSwitch 芯片);NVL72 用 **9 个 tray** 全互联 72 GPU 的各 18 条链路;内置 **SHARP 引擎**做在网归约/组播;域最大可扩至 576 GPU、总带宽 >1 PB/s | Scale-up | [1][2] |
| HGX B300 8-GPU NVLink 域 | Blackwell Ultra | 8× B300 SXM + **2 颗 NVSwitch**(每 GPU 连双 NVSwitch,节点内 all-to-all);GPU-GPU 1.8 TB/s,**聚合 14.4 TB/s**;板载 8× ConnectX-8(每 GPU 800 Gb/s 出口) | Scale-up(节点内) | [10][11] |
| NVLink 6 | Vera Rubin(NVL144,2H2026) | **3.6 TB/s per GPU**(每向 1.8 TB/s);机架聚合 **260 TB/s** | Scale-up | [1][13][14] |
| ConnectX-8 SuperNIC | Blackwell 世代 | **800 Gb/s**(XDR InfiniBand 或 2×400G / 800G Ethernet 双协议);PCIe **Gen6 48 lane** 内置 PCIe switch | Scale-out(E-W) | [8][9] |
| ConnectX-9 | Rubin 世代(2026) | **1.6 Tb/s** per NIC;NVL144 机架 scale-out 聚合 28.8 TB/s | Scale-out(E-W) | [13][14] |
| Quantum-X800(Q3400-RA) | XDR InfiniBand | **144× 800 Gb/s**(72 OSFP 笼),**115.2 Tb/s** 无阻塞;**SHARPv4** 在网计算;200G SerDes;两层 fat-tree 最多接 **10,368 张 CX8**;4U 风冷 | Scale-out(IB) | [6][7] |
| Spectrum-4 SN5600 / SN5610 | Spectrum-X 800GbE | **64× 800GbE OSFP,51.2 Tb/s**,33.3 Bpps,160 MB 共享缓冲,2U;RoCE 扩展 + **自适应路由 + 遥测拥塞控制**(端侧配 CX8/BlueField 生效);SN5610 多一个 25GbE 管理口 | Scale-out(Ethernet)/ N-S 汇聚 | [15][16] |
| BlueField-3(B3240) | 第 3 代 DPU | **400 Gb/s**;NVL72 RA 中位于每计算 tray,承载 CPU 收敛网(存储 + 带内管理)RoCE 卸载 | N-S / 存储 | [4][17] |
| BlueField-4 | 第 4 代 DPU(2026,Vera Rubin 世代) | **800 Gb/s**,算力 6×于前代;AI factory 前端 N-S、存储、安全、多租户「AI 工厂操作系统」载体 | N-S / 存储 | [18] |
| SN2201 | 管理交换机 | 1G BMC 接入 + 100G 上联(RA:每 SU 8×100G + 142×1G) | OOB 管理 | [4] |

Rail-optimized leaf-spine 典型结构(NVL72 RA 实测口径,[3][4]):每 GPU 800 Gb/s 拆成 **2×400G 双平面**;每平面内按 **rail** 组织——同编号 GPU 的 NIC 全部接同一台 leaf(GL,SN5610),4 个 rail × 2 平面;leaf 每 rail 36×400G 下行 + 36×400G 上行到 spine(GS),**两层无阻塞 fat-tree**;单平面可扩至 1024 个 400G 接口。跨节点同 rail 通信只需一跳 leaf,跨 rail 流量先走节点内 NVLink 换轨。

---

## 2. 四张网职责与业务映射表

| 网络 | 流量类型 | 影响指标 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|---|
| ① Scale-up(NVLink/NVSwitch 域) | TP 的 all-reduce/all-gather;NVL72 域内 EP all-to-all(dispatch/combine);同机架 PD 分离的 KV 传输;NVSwitch SHARP 在网归约 | **TPOT**、交互吞吐(tokens/s/GPU) | 1.8 TB/s/GPU,是 800G 网卡(100 GB/s)的 **18×**;72 GPU 域内 all-to-all 每字节成本与 8 GPU 相同 |
| ② Scale-out 计算网(E-W:Quantum-X800 IB 或 Spectrum-X 以太) | 跨机架 DP/PP 梯度同步;跨 NVL72 的 EP all-to-all;跨机架 KV 传输(Dynamo/NIXL);SHARPv4 大规模 all-reduce | 训练线性扩展度、跨机架 **TTFT**、故障重排延迟 | rail-optimized 双平面;每 GPU 800 Gb/s(2×400G) |
| ③ North-South / 存储收敛网 | 模型/checkpoint 加载、数据集读取、用户请求进出、带内管理 | **冷启动时间**、checkpoint 恢复时长、请求首跳 | NVL72 RA:每 tray 2×400G(BlueField-3)接双 SN5600,**每节点存储带宽约 40 GB/s**,RoCE |
| ④ OOB 管理网 | BMC/IPMI、固件升级、监控遥测 | 可运维性、MTTR | 1 Gb/s 接入 SN2201,与业务网物理隔离 |

### 业务映射——可引用数字

- **EP all-to-all → TPOT**:域内 vs 跨节点带宽差 **18×**(1.8 TB/s vs CX8 100 GB/s;CX7 400G 时为 36×)。机架级:NVL72 scale-up 130 TB/s vs 72×800Gb/s scale-out ≈ 7.2 TB/s,同为 **18×**。SemiAnalysis InferenceX 实测:GB200 NVL72 跑 Kimi K2.5 wide-EP(decode 可到 EP16)比 8 卡域 B200(EP4 即触 scale-out 延迟墙)**3.1× 吞吐** [19]。UBEP 论文:all-to-all 延迟降 52.4% 使 TPOT 降 11.1%,证明 TPOT 对 all-to-all 直接敏感 [20]。
- **PD 分离 KV 传输 → TTFT**:分离架构下 TTFT = prefill 计算 + KV 传输 + decode 出首 token,KV 传输在关键路径上;Dynamo 用 NIXL 自动择路(NVLink > IB/RoCE)[21][22]。业界经验:约 **≥90 Gbps** 专用带宽才能让 KV 传输对用户"不可见";AWS EFA 后端实测 ~9.6 GB/s [23]。同 NVL72 机架内 P/D 走 NVLink 时 KV 传输近似免费——这是 NVL72 域大的直接推理红利。
- **TP 为何必须留在 NVLink 域**:TP 每层两次集合通信、消息小频次高,同时吃带宽和延迟;MoE 文献实测同一 all-to-all 任务 NVLink 内 17.65 µs vs 跨节点 151.8 µs(**~8.6×**)[24]。故 TP 度 ≤ NVLink 域(HGX 为 8,NVL72 可到 72)。
- **模型加载 → 冷启动**:走 ③ 号网。RA 口径每节点 40 GB/s:1 TB 权重约 **25 s**;若仅 10GbE(1.25 GB/s)需 **~13 min**——同一动作差两个数量级。

# kv_elems_per_tok: 随 context 线性增长的 KV 元素数/每 token(全层合计)

```python
"""容量模型:workload × 模型 KV 口径 × GPU 规格 × benchmark 锚点 → worker/GPU/机架数。

口径移植自模拟器 src/lib/roofline.ts(prefill 算力瓶颈 / decode 带宽瓶颈,
MFU 0.4 / MBU 0.6 经验值),并扩展四类注意力 KV:MLA 全层增长(GLM)、
KDA+MLA 混合(K3,仅 24 层增长 + 恒定状态)、CSA/HCA 摊销(V4)。
null 纪律:官方没有的口径给区间(low/mid/high),不给伪精确单点。
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import math

from . import params as P


# ---------- 显存 ----------
def kv_bytes_per_token(model_key: str, kv_dtype_bytes: float) -> float:
    m = P.MODELS[model_key]
    return m['kv_elems_per_tok'] * kv_dtype_bytes + m['kv_extra_bytes_per_tok']


def memory_breakdown_gb(model_key: str, concurrency: int, avg_ctx: int,
                        kv_dtype_bytes: float) -> dict:
    """单 worker 显存构成(GB):权重 + KV + 恒定状态 + 运行开销,× 安全系数。"""
    m = P.MODELS[model_key]
    weights = m['total_b'] * m['w_bytes']
    kv = kv_bytes_per_token(model_key, kv_dtype_bytes) * avg_ctx * concurrency / 1e9
    const_state = m['const_state_bytes_per_seq'] * concurrency / 1e9
    overhead = weights * 0.10 + 2.0
    subtotal = weights + kv + const_state + overhead
    return dict(weights=weights, kv=kv, const_state=const_state, overhead=overhead,
                subtotal=subtotal, total=subtotal * P.SAFETY)


def max_concurrency(model_key: str, hw: dict, gpus: int, avg_ctx: int,
                    kv_dtype_bytes: float) -> int:
    """给定 worker(gpus 张卡)与平均 context,显存允许的最大并发序列数。"""
    m = P.MODELS[model_key]
    budget = hw['hbm_gb'] * gpus * P.HBM_USABLE
    weights = m['total_b'] * m['w_bytes']
    fixed = (weights + weights * 0.10 + 2.0) * P.SAFETY
    per_seq = (kv_bytes_per_token(model_key, kv_dtype_bytes) * avg_ctx
               + m['const_state_bytes_per_seq']) / 1e9 * P.SAFETY
    if budget <= fixed:
        return 0
    return int((budget - fixed) / per_seq)


def min_gpus_for_weights(model_key: str, hw: dict) -> int:
    """只放权重(+开销)所需的最少 GPU 数(roofline.ts minGpus 口径)。"""
    m = P.MODELS[model_key]
    weights = m['total_b'] * m['w_bytes']
    total = (weights + weights * 0.10 + 2.0) * P.SAFETY
    return max(1, math.ceil(total / (hw['hbm_gb'] * P.HBM_USABLE)))


# ---------- 吞吐(roofline 兜底,锚点优先) ----------
def roofline_decode_tok_s_per_gpu(model_key: str, hw: dict, batch_per_gpu: int,
                                  avg_ctx: int, kv_dtype_bytes: float,
                                  mbu: float = 0.6) -> float:
    """decode 带宽近似:每步读一遍激活权重(batch 共享)+ batch 份 KV。"""
    m = P.MODELS[model_key]
    weight_bytes = m['active_b'] * 1e9 * m['w_bytes']
    kv_read = kv_bytes_per_token(model_key, kv_dtype_bytes) * avg_ctx * batch_per_gpu
    step_s = (weight_bytes + kv_read) / (hw['bw_tbs'] * 1e12 * mbu)
    return batch_per_gpu / step_s


# ---------- 产能 → 机架数 ----------
def rack_plan(model_key: str, hw: dict = P.GB300_NVL72) -> dict:
    """按设计产能(总吞吐 tpm)推 worker/机架数。

    锚点吞吐为 A2 公开数据的输出 token/s/GPU(PD 分离口径,已含 prefill GPU 摊销);
    输出份额 = 总吞吐 / (1+R)。
    """
    m = P.MODELS[model_key]
    tpm = P.CAPACITY_TPM[model_key]
    out_tok_s = tpm / 60.0 / (1.0 + P.R_IN_OUT)
    anchor = m['anchor_out_tok_s_gpu']
    plan = {}
    for band in ('low', 'mid', 'high'):
        per_rack = anchor[band] * hw['gpus']
        racks_raw = out_tok_s / per_rack / P.PEAK_HEADROOM
        plan[band] = dict(per_rack_out_tok_s=per_rack, racks_raw=racks_raw,
                          racks=max(1, math.ceil(racks_raw)))
    # 保守配置取 low 带的整数机架;mid 供叙事
    return dict(model=m['display'], tpm=tpm, out_tok_s=out_tok_s,
                anchor=anchor, plan=plan,
                racks_committed=plan['low']['racks'],
                gpus_committed=plan['low']['racks'] * hw['gpus'])


def full_plan(hw: dict = P.GB300_NVL72) -> dict:
    per_model = {k: rack_plan(k, hw) for k in P.CAPACITY_TPM}
    racks = sum(v['racks_committed'] for v in per_model.values())
    return dict(per_model=per_model, racks_total=racks,
                gpus_total=racks * hw['gpus'],
                power_kw=racks * (hw['rack_kw'] or 0))


# ---------- p5-x 单 worker 实例 ----------
def worker_example(model_key: str, hw: dict, gpus: int, avg_ctx: int,
                   concurrency: int) -> dict:
    """给定 worker 形态与 workload,输出显存构成与并发上限(BF16/FP8 双 KV 口径)。"""
    out = dict(model=P.MODELS[model_key]['display'], gpus=gpus,
               hbm_budget=hw['hbm_gb'] * gpus * P.HBM_USABLE,
               worker_ref=P.MODELS[model_key]['worker_ref'])
    for label, b in (('kv_fp8', 1), ('kv_bf16', 2)):
        out[label] = dict(
            mem=memory_breakdown_gb(model_key, concurrency, avg_ctx, b),
            max_concurrency=max_concurrency(model_key, hw, gpus, avg_ctx, b),
            kv_kb_per_token=kv_bytes_per_token(model_key, b) / 1024,
        )
    return out


# ---------- 自检(与 A1 / roofline.ts 交叉核对) ----------
def _self_test():
    # GLM-5.2/5.3: 78×576 元素,BF16 ≈ 87.8 KB/token(A1 表)
    glm = kv_bytes_per_token('glm-5.3', 2)
    assert abs(glm / 1024 - (87.75 + 21 * 128 / 1024)) < 0.5, glm
    # DeepSeek-V3 对照(roofline.ts 口径):61 层×576×2B = 70.3KB —— 公式一致性
    dsv3 = 576 * 61 * 2 / 1024
    assert abs(dsv3 - 68.6) < 0.5, dsv3
    # K3: 24×512×2B = 24 KB/token(A1)
    assert abs(kv_bytes_per_token('kimi-k3', 2) / 1024 - 24.0) < 0.1
    # V4-Pro BF16 ≈ 9.8 KB/token(A1)
    assert abs(kv_bytes_per_token('dsv4-pro', 2) / 1024 - 9.62) < 0.5
    # K3 权重必须放得下 8×B300(Fixstars 实测 ~196GB/GPU)
    w = memory_breakdown_gb('kimi-k3', 0, 0, 2)['weights']
    assert 1500 < w < 1650, w


if __name__ == '__main__':
    _self_test()
    import json
    print(json.dumps(full_plan(), indent=1, ensure_ascii=False, default=str))

```

```python
"""财务模型:5 年营收 / 成本 / 利润 + 敏感性矩阵。

slide 公式(p2):
  年收入 = Σ_模型 [ Q_out×P_out + Q_in×( h×P_cached + (1−h)×P_in ) ]
    其中 Q_out = C_tpm × U × 525,600(min/年) ÷ (1+R),Q_in = Q_out × R
  年利润 = 年收入 − CapEx/T_dep − 电费(P_rack×PUE×N_rack×8760×电价) − 托管 − 运维
所有参数见 params.py(单一来源);单价按年衰减 PRICE_EROSION_PER_YEAR。
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os

from . import capacity_model as C
from . import params as P

MIN_PER_YEAR = 60 * 24 * 365  # 525,600


def revenue_year(model_key: str, utilization: float, year_idx: int) -> dict:
    tpm = P.CAPACITY_TPM[model_key]
    pr = P.PRICES[model_key]
    decay = P.PRICE_EROSION_PER_YEAR ** year_idx
    total_tokens = tpm * MIN_PER_YEAR * utilization          # 总吞吐口径(已确认)
    q_out = total_tokens / (1 + P.R_IN_OUT)
    q_in = q_out * P.R_IN_OUT
    rev_out = q_out / 1e6 * pr['output'] * decay
    rev_in = q_in / 1e6 * (P.CACHE_HIT * pr['cached']
                           + (1 - P.CACHE_HIT) * pr['input']) * decay
    return dict(tokens_t=total_tokens / 1e12, out=rev_out, inp=rev_in,
                total=rev_out + rev_in)


def cost_year(racks: int, rack_price_musd: float) -> dict:
    capex = racks * rack_price_musd * 1e6 * (1 + P.BOM_ADDER)
    dep = capex / P.DEP_YEARS
    kw = racks * P.GB300_NVL72['rack_kw'] * P.PUE
    power = kw * 8760 * P.ELEC_USD_PER_KWH
    colo = racks * P.GB300_NVL72['rack_kw'] * P.COLO_USD_PER_KW_MONTH * 12
    return dict(capex=capex, dep=dep, power=power, colo=colo, ops=P.OPS_USD_PER_YEAR,
                total=dep + power + colo + P.OPS_USD_PER_YEAR)


def five_year(rack_price_musd: float | None = None,
              utilization_ramp: list | None = None) -> dict:
    price = rack_price_musd or P.GB300_NVL72['price_musd']['mid']
    ramp = utilization_ramp or P.UTILIZATION_RAMP
    cap = C.full_plan()
    racks = cap['racks_total']
    years = []
    for y in range(P.YEARS):
        per_model = {k: revenue_year(k, ramp[y], y) for k in P.CAPACITY_TPM}
        rev = sum(v['total'] for v in per_model.values())
        cost = cost_year(racks, price)
        years.append(dict(year=2027 + y, utilization=ramp[y],
                          revenue=rev, cost=cost['total'], profit=rev - cost['total'],
                          per_model=per_model))
    cost0 = cost_year(racks, price)
    return dict(racks=racks, gpus=cap['gpus_total'], power_kw=cap['power_kw'],
                rack_price_musd=price, capex=cost0['capex'],
                cost_breakdown_y1=cost0, years=years,
                cum_profit=sum(y['profit'] for y in years))


def breakeven_utilization(rack_price_musd: float, year_idx: int = 2) -> float | None:
    """给定机架单价,第 year_idx 年(默认第 3 年价位)收支平衡所需利用率。"""
    cap = C.full_plan()
    cost = cost_year(cap['racks_total'], rack_price_musd)['total']
    rev_at_full = sum(revenue_year(k, 1.0, year_idx)['total'] for k in P.CAPACITY_TPM)
    if rev_at_full <= 0:
        return None
    u = cost / rev_at_full
    return u if u <= 1.0 else None


def sensitivity() -> list:
    """机架单价 × 稳态利用率 → 第 3 年利润(百万美元)。"""
    rows = []
    for price in (P.GB300_NVL72['price_musd']['low'], P.GB300_NVL72['price_musd']['mid'],
                  P.GB300_NVL72['price_musd']['high']):
        row = dict(rack_price=price, cells={})
        for u in (0.25, 0.40, 0.60):
            fy = five_year(price, [u] * P.YEARS)
            row['cells'][u] = fy['years'][2]['profit'] / 1e6
        row['breakeven_u'] = breakeven_utilization(price)
        rows.append(row)
    return rows


def main():
    out = dict(base=five_year(), sensitivity=sensitivity(),
               capacity=C.full_plan())
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), 'out'), exist_ok=True)
    path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), 'out', 'results.json')
    with open(path, 'w') as f:
        json.dump(out, f, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False, default=str)
    b = out['base']
    print(f"racks={b['racks']} gpus={b['gpus']} capex=${b['capex']/1e6:.0f}M "
          f"(rack @${b['rack_price_musd']}M +{P.BOM_ADDER:.0%} BOM)")
    for y in b['years']:
        print(f"  {y['year']} U={y['utilization']:.0%}: rev ${y['revenue']/1e6:7.1f}M "
              f"cost ${y['cost']/1e6:6.1f}M profit ${y['profit']/1e6:7.1f}M")
    print(f"  5 年累计利润 ${b['cum_profit']/1e6:.0f}M")
    for r in out['sensitivity']:
        cells = '  '.join(f"U{u:.0%}: {v:7.1f}M" for u, v in r['cells'].items())
        be = f"盈亏平衡 U={r['breakeven_u']:.1%}" if r['breakeven_u'] else '全区间亏损'
        print(f"  rack ${r['rack_price']}M → {cells} | {be}")


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

```

## Storage Performance Requirements

For certain workloads, 4 GBps per GPU of read performance is required, specifically for use cases like computer vision tasks with high-resolution images. For NLP and LLM cases, peak performance for reads and writes are needed for creating and reading checkpoint files, and at least ½ of the read performance is recommended as write performance for LLM and large model use cases.

For H100-based systems, a GDS-enabled application should be able to read data at over 40 GBps directly into the GPUs.

## Certified Storage Partners

The search results mention that Pure Storage earned NVIDIA certification for NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD with DGX GB200 or DGX GB300 Systems. Another certified partner mentioned is VAST Data. However, the search results indicate that the approach to certification is holistic: can the storage system provide a level of performance to keep a SuperPOD busy and meet Nvidia's latency criteria, sustained performance levels, scalability to support thousands of GPUs, and large AI dataset handling, rather than focusing solely on per-GPU bandwidth metrics.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about Run:ai Model Streamer benchmarks for model loading times with safetensors:

## Benchmark Overview

The Run:ai Model Streamer benchmarks present performance analysis highlighting effectiveness across different storage types (local SSDs and cloud-based S3), compared against other tools like the Hugging Face safetensors loader and Tensorizer.

## Performance Results

As concurrency increases, load times decrease significantly, dropping from 28.24 seconds (at concurrency 4) to 4.88 seconds (at concurrency 32).

The Model Streamer significantly reduces model loading times, outperforming traditional methods by leveraging concurrent streaming and optimized storage throughput, benchmarked against other loaders such as the Hugging Face Safetensors Loader and CoreWeave Tensorizer across various storage types, including local SSDs and Amazon S3.

## Support for Cloud Storage

The Model Streamer supports loading from both S3 and GCS:
- The streamer supports GCS URLs when using HMAC authentication (e.g., gs://my-bucket/my/file/path.safetensors).
- It can accelerate loading large AI model weights from Cloud Storage by using Run:ai Model Streamer with the vLLM inference server, assuming models and weights are in safetensors format in a Cloud Storage bucket.

For detailed benchmark methodology and results, you can refer to the official benchmark documentation on the Run:ai Model Streamer GitHub repository.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about NVIDIA Dynamo KVBM KV cache offload with NVMe SSD tiering and TTFT benchmarks:

## KVBM Overview

The Dynamo KV Block Manager (KVBM) is a scalable runtime component designed to handle memory allocation, management, and remote sharing of Key-Value (KV) blocks for inference tasks across heterogeneous and distributed environments, acting as a unified memory layer for frameworks like vLLM and TensorRT-LLM.

## KV Cache Tiering with NVMe

KV cache offloading extends GPU HBM capacity with CPU DRAM and NVMe SSDs, resulting in the two-tier HBM-DRAM and three-tier HBM-DRAM-SSD hierarchies. When disk offloading is enabled, disk offload filtering is enabled by default to extend SSD lifespan, with the current policy only offloading KV blocks from CPU to disk if the blocks have frequency ≥ 2.

## TTFT Benchmarking

LMBenchmark can be used to evaluate KVBM performance, with average TTFT and other performance numbers in the output. When a user session is reactivated, the TTFT for that specific re-activated user/conversation is entirely bound by how fast the offloaded KV cache data can be retrieved.

## Performance Improvements

Real-world benchmarks show significant improvements: VAST collaborated with CoreWeave to evaluate NVIDIA's Dynamo KV cache offload and saw GPU efficiency improve by 90% and TTFT improve by 20x as compared to when GPUs need to prefill calculate every past context.

## Power Requirements

The GB300 NVL72 draws 132-142 kW per rack, with peaks near 155 kW. HPE recommends provisioning busway capacity for 192 kW to absorb transients.

## Rack Weight

The rack weighs 1,580 kg fully populated on a 0.641 m² footprint.

## Power Distribution Architecture

Row-level busway distribution (Starline, Legrand, or equivalent) is required. Industry best practice involves provisioning dual 415V three-phase feeds per rack via 160A IEC 60309 connectors, which cuts I²R losses by 75% compared to 208V while maintaining compatibility with European facility standards.

Internally it runs a single-zone 50 VDC busbar rated 1,400 A, fed by eight power shelves at 33 kW each, one 60 A whip per shelf across four AC buses.

## Facility Requirements

Key facility requirements include:

- **Power**: The facility must provide redundant power feeds capable of sustaining this load continuously, with sufficient headroom for transient spikes during GPU initialization and stress testing
- **Floor Loading**: With 2,200 to 2,470 kg/m² of point load, most existing data halls are between 1.6 and 2.4 times under TIA-942's recommended raised floor rating
- **Cooling**: 100% liquid cooling is required with CDU connection to facility chilled water at 30-40°C supply, water filtered to 50 microns, conductivity monitoring, and corrosion inhibitors
- **Space**: Verify aisle width, overhead clearance for coolant manifolds, and door swing clearance before delivery, as some facilities have had to remove door frames to get NVL72 racks into position

Based on the search results, here's relevant information about LMCache, Mooncake, and KV cache performance:

## LMCache and Mooncake Integration

LMCache works as a KV connector and tiered storage layer that serializes KV tensors into a tiered store (GPU HBM, CPU DRAM, NVMe, Redis).

## Storage Tiers and Throughput Requirements

CPU DRAM serves as a warm tier that captures recently-evicted HBM blocks, while NVMe functions as a cold tier when disk throughput exceeds 4 GB/s sequential.

## TTFT Improvement

LMCache cuts TTFT from 11s to 1.5s on 128K-context workloads by sharing KV cache across vLLM nodes. Additionally, under stress with 32 users on 100k context agentic traces, LMCache delivers 3.0× lower TTFT average and 2.1× lower p95.

## Mooncake Architecture

Mooncake is an open-source distributed KV cache storage system that creates a distributed memory pool by aggregating memory space from various client nodes, pooling underutilized DRAM and SSD resources from multiple nodes. Experiments show that Mooncake achieves up to a 525% throughput increase in simulated scenarios while meeting SLOs.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about NVIDIA NIM model loading, cold start times, and LLM inference autoscaling:

## Cold Start Times

Scaling an LLM from zero means full container initialization, loading model weights from disk, and allocating GPU memory; a process that can take tens of seconds to minutes. More specifically, a 70B model cold start on an uncached container can easily hit 6-10 minutes total, while even with pre-pulled images, 60-90 seconds is common.

## Why Cold Starts Are Slow

A 70B model in fp16 is about 140 GB, and loading that takes tens of seconds from fast local disk and minutes over a network before the engine is even ready.

## Solutions and Optimizations

With NVIDIA Run:ai, NIM deployments get inference-first prioritization, GPU fractions with full memory isolation, smarter placement based on workload needs, dynamic memory management, and autoscaling (including replica scaling and scale-to-zero).

NVIDIA Run:ai Model Streamer is an open source Python SDK designed to mitigate these issues by concurrently reading model weights from storage and streaming them directly into GPU memory. Additionally, GPU memory swap delivers 44-61x faster TTFT than scale-from-zero while using fewer resources when combined with GPU fractions.

## Autoscaling Challenges

Cold starts can take several minutes, as a new replica has to be placed on a GPU node, pull tens of gigabytes of weights, load them into VRAM, and warm up.

## Retrofit Timelines

Retrofitting an air-cooled facility to support high-density liquid-cooled racks takes 12–18 months of civil and mechanical work. However, phased approaches can accelerate portions of this timeline. Notable example: A pharmaceutical company retrofitting a 2008-era facility for 800 NVIDIA H100 GPUs completed the work in four months at $4.2 million—versus $35 million for new construction taking 18 months.

## New Build AI Data Center Construction Timeline

Developers are adopting modular construction and digital twin technology to shrink traditional 24–36 month timelines down to just 12–14 months.

## Market Growth in 2025

The data center liquid cooling market reached $5.52 billion in 2025 and is forecast to hit $15.75 billion by 2030. Additionally, every new AI data center is expected to be fully liquid-cooled within the next two to three years.

Based on the search results, here's comprehensive information about NVIDIA GenAI-Perf metrics:

## GenAI-Perf Overview

GenAI-Perf is a command line tool for measuring the throughput and latency of generative AI models as served through an inference server. It is a client-side LLM-focused benchmarking tool, providing key metrics such as TTFT, ITL, TPS, RPS and more.

## Key Metrics

### Time to First Token (TTFT)
Time to first token (TTFT) is the time it takes to process the prompt and generate the first token. In other words, it measures how long a user must wait before seeing the model's output. TTFT generally includes both request queuing time, prefill time, and network latency.

### Inter-Token Latency (ITL) / Time Per Output Token (TPOT)
Intertoken latency (ITL) is the average time between the generation of consecutive tokens in a sequence. It is also known as time per output token (TPOT). GenAI-Perf does not include TTFT and is defined as: ITL = (e2e_latency - TTFT) / (Total_output_tokens - 1)

### Additional Metrics
For large language models (LLMs), GenAI-Perf provides metrics such as output token throughput, time to first token, inter token latency, and request throughput.

## Visualization Capabilities
GenAI-Perf can also generate various plots that visualize the performance of the current profile run. This is disabled by default but users can easily enable it by passing the --generate-plots option.

Based on the search results, here's information about the key concepts:

## Goodput Definition

Goodput is defined as the number of requests served per second while meeting the latency targets (p99), allowing a maximum of 1% of total requests to violate their SLO. In other words, it measures throughput with quality-of-service constraints enforced.

## DistServe's Goodput-Optimized Performance

DistServe maximizes the per-GPU goodput – the maximum request rate that can be served adhering to the SLO attainment goal for each GPU provisioned, resulting in up to 4.48x lower cost per LLM query with guaranteed satisfaction of SLOs.

DistServe demonstrates "Goodput-Optimized Performance" for LLM serving by achieving substantial performance gains, including a 7.4x increase in requests and 12.6x tighter SLOs compared to vLLM.

DistServe's technical optimization prioritizes goodput to minimize cost per query by intelligently optimizing GPU utilization while adhering to Time To First Token (TTFT) and Time Per Output Token (TPOT) constraints.

## Architecture Approach

DistServe is a new LLM serving architecture that disaggregates the prefill and decoding computation, which allows it to optimize resource utilization differently for the compute-heavy prefill phase and memory-heavy decoding phase.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about SemiAnalysis InferenceMAX methodology:

## Overview

SemiAnalysis InferenceMAX applies a Pareto frontier methodology to evaluate the trade-off between responsiveness and throughput, mapping Blackwell's performance envelope across real-world operating conditions.

## Pareto Frontier Concept

InferenceMAX uses the Pareto frontier — a curve that shows the best trade-offs between different factors, such as data center throughput and responsiveness — to map performance. More specifically, a Pareto frontier contains the operating points for which no other measured point is better on both compared dimensions. For throughput versus interactivity, a point is dominated if another point serves more total tokens and also streams faster to each user. Removing dominated points leaves the efficient boundary of the measured configurations.

## Throughput and Interactivity Trade-off

The real challenge lies in optimizing the Pareto frontier: the curve that represents the best possible trade-off between Tokens Per Second (TPS) per GPU (TCO, total cost of ownership) and TPS per User (interactivity). Pushing this curve upwards and to the right means delivering faster generation for individual users while allowing more users to share the hardware.

Throughput is measured in tok/s/gpu and is best obtained by serving many clients at once, as LLM inference relies on matrix multiplication, which benefits from batching many requests. However, serving many requests at once lowers how much time the GPU can dedicate to a single one, so getting faster output means increasing interactivity (measured as tok/s/user) and lowering throughput.

The InferenceMAX benchmark is now also referred to as InferenceX and continues to evolve as an open-source, vendor-neutral benchmarking platform.

# Storage Performance Requirements for DGX SuperPOD

## Performance Tiers

The documentation defines two performance tiers:

**Standard:** Supports "multiple concurrent LLM or fine-tuning training jobs" where datasets fit in local memory cache and involve single-modality models with millions of parameters.

**Enhanced:** Handles "multiple concurrent multimodal training jobs" with datasets too large for cache, requiring billions+ parameter models.

## Bandwidth Specifications

| Metric | Standard | Enhanced |
|--------|----------|----------|
| Single SU read | 80 GBps | 250 GBps |
| Single SU write | 40 GBps | 124 GBps |
| 8 SU read aggregate | 640 GBps | 2,000 GBps |
| 8 SU write aggregate | 320 GBps | 992 GBps |

## Per-GPU Guidance

The document recommends "4 GBps per GPU of read performance" for computer vision tasks using high-resolution images exceeding 30 TB.

## Local NVMe Role

DGX B300 systems include local NVMe storage "that can also be used for caching or staging data," reducing network retrieval needs.

## Write Performance

For large model checkpoints, the guidance suggests "at least ½ of the read performance as recommended write performance for LLM" use cases.

**Note:** The documentation does not specify capacity guidance per SU or GPU.

The search returned comprehensive results about VAST Data's VUA (VAST Undivided Attention) technology. Here's a summary of the key findings:

## Overview

VAST Data announced the availability of their open-source, global exabyte-scale key-value service called VAST Undivided Attention (VUA).

## Core Functionality

VUA is open-source KVCache software technology that stores generated AI model training and inferencing tokens in NVMe-connected SSDs for fast transfer to GPU memory to avoid recomputing them. VUA integrates with popular AI inference workloads and expands cache space to a third tier of persistent, shared NVMe memory, providing infinite context scalability.

## Performance Benefits

By leveraging NVIDIA GPU Direct Storage (GDS) and RDMA-based protocols, VUA facilitates direct, high-speed data transfers between shared NVMe storage and GPU memory, bypassing CPU bottlenecks. VUA supports popular frameworks like vLLM, LMCache, and NVIDIA's Dynamo, significantly reducing Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) for context-sharing requests and maximizing GPU utilization.

## GPU Server Integration

Each GPU server now has shared access to the same extended context cache space, the same rapidly-searchable metadata space and the same global context and attention data.

## Industry Adoption

The general architectural approach of offloading KV cache to NVMe SSDs has been implemented by Hammerspace, VAST Data with VUA, and WEKA.

Based on the web search results, here are key findings about Milvus vector database RAG retrieval latency and its impact on end-to-end LLM performance:

## P99 Latency Impact on RAG Systems

One case study showed a RAG pipeline that cut p99 latency from 1.8 seconds to 190ms by co-locating all three components on the same GPU server. Total round trip for embed + search + LLM TTFT should be under 50ms on H100 SXM5 at this configuration.

## Retrieval as a System Bottleneck

Most production RAG pipelines split their vector database and LLM inference across two separate services, and every query crosses two network boundaries: one to the vector database (30-250ms p99) and one to the LLM API (100-600ms p99).

In production RAG systems, end-to-end latency is often dominated by retrieval operations—embedding computation, vector database queries, network round-trips, and optional re-ranking.

## GPU Acceleration Benefits

NVIDIA CAGRA (graph-based ANN on GPU) builds a 100M-vector index in minutes versus hours on CPU, and GPU-IVF flat search delivers 10-50x higher QPS on the same hardware. Every vector database co-located with an LLM inference server benefits from GPU vectorization—embedding throughput on H100 is 100x faster than CPU.

## Monitoring Retrieval Performance

For example, if the retriever averages 150 ms at 50 QPS but the LLM processes 200 QPS, the retriever becomes the bottleneck.

## Overview

Meta developed an AI-assisted root cause analysis system that uses a combination of heuristic-based retrieval and large language model-based ranking to speed up root cause identification during investigations.

## Key Performance Metric

The system achieves 42% accuracy in identifying root causes for investigations at their creation time related to Meta's web monorepo. Based on exhaustive backtesting with historical investigations and the information available at their start, 42% of these investigations had the root cause in the top five suggested code changes.

## Technical Approach

The system combines heuristic-based retrieval with LLM-based ranking to identify potential root causes of incidents. The team fine-tuned their Llama 2 model with 5,000 instruction-tuning examples, which helped the system rank potential code changes based on investigation relevance.

## Safety Measures

To mitigate risks of suggesting incorrect root causes, Meta prioritizes closed feedback loops, result explainability, and confidence measurement methodologies.

## Source

The information comes from Meta's engineering blog article titled "Leveraging AI for efficient incident response" published in June 2024.

Based on the search results, here's what I found regarding liquid cooling versus air cooling for AI data centers:

## PUE Comparison

Air cooling typically achieves PUE of 1.4-1.8, while liquid cooling achieves PUE of 1.05-1.15 regardless of ambient conditions. Direct-to-chip cooling eliminates 80% of the thermal resistance between GPU dies and cooling systems, dropping data center PUE from 1.58 to 1.15.

## Market Adoption in 2025

22% of data centers now implement liquid cooling systems, and direct-to-chip cooling commands a dominant 47% market share. The data center liquid cooling market reached $5.52 billion in 2025 and is forecast to hit $15.75 billion by 2030 (23.31% CAGR).

## Performance Advantages

Liquid cooling supports 100-200 kW per rack—5x density improvement compared to air cooling's hard limit of 41.3 kW per rack. Liquid cooling is up to 3,000 times more effective than using air cooling, enabling higher compute density while reducing energy usage.

## Industry Transition

Microsoft began fleet deployment across Azure campuses in July 2025, marking a significant shift toward liquid cooling as standard infrastructure rather than a niche technology.

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values — touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe — run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure — do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job — magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). → `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) — each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. → `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette — run the script, don't reason about ΔE.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,…>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory — or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, ≥8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. → `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer — by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. → `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For ≥ 2 series a legend is always present and ≤ 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box — the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** — its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout — open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** — it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue — it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale → two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake — see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light→dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD ΔE ≥ 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6–8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL — full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead — see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view — it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for ≥ 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** — values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance — every value filled in — is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical — steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of — build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong — check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** — every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |

# Storage in NVIDIA's Inference Reference Architecture

## Storage Architecture Overview

The RA distinguishes multiple storage tiers for inference workloads: "Model artifacts often start in object or file storage. Hot models may need node-local cache, shared cache, or GPU-to-GPU transfer paths."

## Storage Tiers and Purposes

**Persistent vs. Ephemeral**: The architecture separates "persistent model artifact storage from ephemeral cache and from telemetry retention." Storage domains serve distinct functions:

- Model artifact storage (object, file, block)
- Cache storage (hot models, KV blocks)
- Benchmark output and telemetry retention
- Container image cache
- Local ephemeral capacity

## Local NVMe Guidance

Node-local NVMe supports "image cache, model cache, temporary tensors, and short-lived logs when that capability is part of the provider handoff." The architecture treats local storage as a planned tier, not emergency overflow.

## Model Loading and Movement

**Cold Start Performance**: The RA emphasizes decomposing model startup into distinct phases: "artifact discovery, cache warmup, weight movement, container startup, backend initialization, and first-ready signaling." Teams should track model download time, cache-hit time, peer-transfer time, and container ready time separately.

**Acceleration Components**: ModelExpress, NIXL, Velo, FlexTensor, and Run:ai Model Streamer address bottlenecks where "model load time, weight movement, tensor staging, large payload movement, or memory-tier pressure" constrain scaling.

## Key Sections Covering Storage

- *Data Center Architecture* → Storage Domain
- *Inference Serving Flow*
- *Model Data And Memory Architecture*
- *Common Component Combinations* (Model Data Plane Acceleration)
- *Getting Started* guidance

## NVIDIA NIM LLM Benchmarking Guide Overview

This guide helps large language model application developers and system owners benchmark inference latency and throughput for NVIDIA NIM deployments, covering key metrics, test parameters, and a hands-on walkthrough with AIPerf.

## Recommended Benchmarking Tools

Standardized benchmarking of LLM performance can be done with many tools, including Locust and K6, along with NVIDIA AIPerf. AIPerf is NVIDIA's recommended benchmarking tool for generative AI inference.

## Key Metrics Covered

The guide covers important performance metrics including:
- End-to-end request latency, which measures how long it takes from submitting a query to receiving the full response, including queueing, batching, and network latency
- Time to First Token (TTFT)
- Inter-token Latency (ITL)
- Tokens Per Second (TPS)
- Requests Per Second (RPS)

I found comprehensive information about LLM inference benchmarking related to prefix caching and cache hit rates. Here are the key findings:

## Cache Hit Rate Variability Across Workloads

Different workloads have substantially different prefix cache demands—multi-turn conversational scenarios achieve prefix cache hit rates of 90.7%, while tasks like summarization or code completion typically present distinct contexts with hit rates of 6.3% and 0.1%, respectively. This demonstrates a critical pitfall: **benchmark results are highly dependent on the workload type**.

## Production vs. Benchmark Limitations

In production, prefix cache hit rate should be treated as a per-workload metric rather than a single global number. This highlights that benchmarking with a single synthetic prompt distribution may not represent the diverse workload patterns seen in production systems.

## Incomplete Benchmark Coverage

There's a lack of opinionated and reliable ways of benchmarking KV cache reuse performance, with requirements including configuration of prefix reuse ratio, diversity of content type and sequence length, variable request arrival rates, and the ability to measure cache hit rates across different request patterns. Many benchmarks fail to capture these realistic conditions.

## Cache Invalidation Issues

The cache may be invalidated with minor changes to prompts, potentially limiting application depending on the service environment, and even minor prompt changes can invalidate the cache. Benchmarks that don't account for minor prompt variations may overestimate real-world cache performance.

These findings suggest key pitfalls: using non-representative prompt distributions, treating cache hit rate as a global metric rather than per-workload, and failing to simulate realistic prompt variation patterns in production systems.

Based on the search results, here are the key findings about speculative decoding acceptance rates in real production traffic compared to benchmarks:

## Gap Between Benchmarks and Real Production Traffic

Real-world acceptance lengths were lower than ideal despite achieving ~2× speedups. Acceptance rates were likely in the 0.6–0.8 range, not the near-perfect theoretical values shown in benchmarks.

In practice, the speedup was lower than expected. This gap exists because benchmark numbers were measured at batch size 1–4 with long outputs and high acceptance rates—the regime where speculative decoding was designed to shine.

## Why Acceptance Rates Drop in Production

Enabling speculative decoding requires monitoring acceptance rates per traffic segment and debugging degraded performance when the acceptance rate drops on a new request distribution. Acceptance behavior depends on the structure and predictability of actual model outputs, so task-based prompts provide a more representative view of practical performance.

Additionally, when speculative decoding is combined with reasoning parsers and structured output constraints (JSON schemas, regex grammars), tokens can be silently dropped during batch verification and the constraint enforcement never completes correctly.

## Recommendations

Before enabling speculative decoding in production, always benchmark performance under your workload, and representative workload measurements and acceptance metrics are needed when selecting a deployment configuration.

## FinOps for AI Definition

FinOps for AI is the practice of applying visibility, allocation, and optimization to AI workloads like LLM token costs, GPU compute, and inference APIs. Defined by the FinOps Foundation, it adapts the standard Inform-Optimize-Operate lifecycle to the specific cost drivers of AI: GPU hardware scarcity, token-based billing, model training economics, and inference infrastructure that scales with user adoption rather than provisioning decisions.

## Practitioner Roles

No single team can manage it alone because cost decisions happen at multiple levels—from model selection in code to infrastructure provisioning to budget approval, and FinOps practitioners serve as central coordinators. FinOps teams managing public cloud costs have been asked to additionally manage technology spending and usage for AI.

## Key GPU Cost Optimization Strategies

Practitioners should regularly track and review AI costs and usage, set quotas, tag resources, and optimize GPU allocation to tightly control AI spending. The FinOps Foundation's AI working group recommends tracking GPU utilization, cost per token, and commitment coverage as core KPIs.

## Certification

The FinOps Foundation announced a dedicated FinOps for AI certification track in November 2025, representing the first industry-recognized credential specifically for AI cost management, with phased content release through March 2026.

## Build Timeline

xAI and Supermicro partnered with Dell Technologies to build the Colossus data center in 122 days, requiring parallel workstreams across facility preparation, power infrastructure, cooling systems, and compute deployment. This 122-day construction shattered the original 24-month timeline. The first major system was built in about 122 days, and then doubled to roughly 200,000 GPUs in another 92 days.

## Facility & Scale

Colossus 1 was built at the former Electrolux factory in South Memphis, with the initial cluster of approximately 100,000 Nvidia H100 GPUs completed in 122 days. As of December 2025, Colossus comprises 150,000 H100 + 50,000 H200 + 30,000 GB200 GPUs—the world's largest single-coherent AI training cluster.

## Liquid Cooling System

The 100,000-GPU cluster uses HGX servers containing eight GPUs each, housed in Supermicro liquid-cooled racks with 64 GPUs per rack, with Supermicro's 4U liquid-cooled systems providing thermal management. Colossus employs a custom liquid-cooling design developed with Supermicro, with each rack housing 64 GPUs and integrating a Cooling Distribution Unit (CDU) that circulates coolant to manage heat.

## Power & Resources

The facility draws 250MW from the Memphis utility grid. The facility draws up to 1.3 million gallons of water daily from the Memphis Aquifer for cooling, about 3% of the local wellfield's capacity.

Based on the search results, here are the key findings regarding reasoning model benchmark TTFT and thinking tokens:

## TTFT Methodology for Reasoning Models

To measure LLM Inference performance of reasoning models, TTFT needs to be measured up to the first reasoning token instead of the first answer token.

Time to First Answer Token is defined as the time in seconds between sending a request and receiving the first answer token, but for reasoning models, this is measured after any 'thinking' time.

## Counting Thinking Tokens

Several benchmarking approaches address how thinking tokens are counted:

- The max tokens are the total output tokens the model can generate (including thinking tokens), while the thinking budget captures only the chain-of-thought or reasoning related tokens.

- Average Reasoning Tokens measures time reasoning models spend outputting 'reasoning' tokens before providing an answer, calculated based on the average number of 'reasoning' tokens across a diverse set of 60 prompts.

## Performance Metrics

A fixed Requests-per-second (RPS) is used to generate outputs to determine average time to first token and inter-token latency, with repeated runs ramping the RPS up until the model's performance passes maximum TTFT and ITL.

These methodological considerations are important because reasoning models have fundamentally different characteristics than standard LLMs, with significantly longer inference times due to extended thinking phases before generating answers.

I've completed the web search for "GPU cluster burn-in testing acceptance validation NVIDIA NCCL stress test". Here are the key findings:

## GPU Burn-In Testing Overview

Traditional node validation methods such as GPU burn-in tests and NCCL communication tests are widely used in large-scale distributed training systems to verify basic hardware functionality before admitting nodes into production clusters.

## NCCL Testing for Validation

NCCL tests help identify numerous issues: by validating the entire cluster, you can find individual nodes, leaf switches, or spine switches that may be having an issue. Testing can scale from individual nodes, to pairs of nodes, to groups of nodes, to the entire cluster in order to quickly determine if there are any faults with Infiniband or GPU Direct RDMA.

A single workflow can verify GPU-to-GPU communication on the cluster before running training, inference, or other production workloads.

## Limitations of Traditional Testing

Traditional methods are primarily designed to detect hard failures and short-term instability, rather than sustained performance degradation under realistic training workloads. GPU burn-in tests focus on exercising compute units using synthetic arithmetic and memory-intensive kernels over short durations. While effective at detecting faults such as overheating or defective cores, they do not sufficiently stress performance-critical subsystems including memory bandwidth, NVLink interconnects, and PCIe paths.

## Pre-Production Validation Strategy

Before running nccl-tests, ensure environment variables match the production configuration. For InfiniBand clusters, set appropriate flags for GPUDirect RDMA. A failing or low-bandwidth NCCL run is much cheaper to diagnose than burning GPU-hours on a misconfigured stack.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about AI infrastructure platform team roles and their division of responsibility:

## Key Roles in AI Infrastructure Teams

Platform teams are now integrating new specialist roles like AI engineers, data engineers, and MLOps specialists. The typical structure includes:

**Platform Engineers**: ML platform engineers build the thing every ML engineer at the company runs on, the paved road that turns a six week deployment into a config change.

**Inference/Model Serving Specialists**: Inference infrastructure specialists focus on containerized serving, latency budgets, canary routing, keeping the endpoint up when traffic spikes.

**MLOps Engineers**: An ML engineer builds models. An MLOps engineer keeps them running in production. MLOps engineers, inference optimization specialists, model serving architects, and data pipeline engineers configure the software layer that actually runs the AI, tuning batch sizes, managing model versioning, setting up A/B serving infrastructure, and monitoring GPU utilization rates.

**SREs**: SRE roles (2-3 positions) handle platform reliability, uptime, and incident response.

**AI Platform Engineers**: AI platform engineers typically have 5+ years in ML infrastructure, MLOps, or platform engineering with GPU workload experience, are familiar with AI coding agents and agentic workflows, and often come from an ML engineering or cloud infrastructure background with hands-on LLM deployment experience.

## Division of Responsibility

Platform teams need to deliver Inference-as-a-Service, abstracting away the complexities of GPU drivers, model versioning, and environment setup, with the platform team's job being to make the hard stuff disappear so people closest to the business problem can move fast.

```text
# KVBM Architecture & Performance Analysis

## Cache Tier Hierarchy

KVBM implements a **three-tier offloading strategy**:

1. **GPU (HBM)** - Primary compute layer
2. **CPU (DRAM)** - Pinned host memory via `DYN_KVBM_CPU_CACHE_GB`
3. **Disk (SSD)** - Persistent storage via `DYN_KVBM_DISK_CACHE_GB`

The documentation notes: *"GPU -> CPU offloading"* as the standard option, with the ability to configure *"GPU -> CPU -> Disk tiered offloading"* or experimental *"GPU -> Disk direct offloading."*

## Bandwidth & Latency

The guide does not provide explicit bandwidth or latency specifications per tier. No numerical performance comparisons (e.g., GB/s transfer rates) are included.

## Benchmark Results

The document references **LMBenchmark** for evaluation but supplies only qualitative guidance rather than actual results. It states that *"Average TTFT and other performance numbers will be in the output"* after running benchmarks, though concrete metrics are absent from this guide.

## Disk Offload Filtering Policy

KVBM implements a frequency-based filtering mechanism: *"only offloads KV blocks from CPU to disk if the blocks have frequency ≥ 2."* The frequency model works as follows:
- Initializes at 1
- Doubles on cache hit
- Decrements by 1 per time decay step

This protects SSD lifespan by limiting writes to frequently-accessed blocks.

## Remote/Shared Storage Integration

The documentation mentions **NIXL** as the compatible storage backend for hierarchical caching. SGLang's HiCache can integrate with *"Dynamo's memory infrastructure"* when using NIXL, enabling storage beyond GPU memory. However, the guide lacks details on vendor plugin extensibility or remote storage protocols.

"""matplotlib 图表生成(白底,配色已过 dataviz 验证器:蓝/琥珀/teal/紫固定序)。

产出到 assets/charts/,由 content 页面引用;数字全部来自 calc,不手抄。
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt  # noqa: E402

from . import capacity_model as C  # noqa: E402
from . import financial_model as F  # noqa: E402

# dataviz 验证过的类别序(勿改顺序)
BLUE, AMBER, TEAL, PURPLE = '#1D4ED8', '#D97706', '#0D9488', '#7C3AED'
INK, DIMC, GRID = '#16202B', '#5F6B7A', '#E6EAF0'
OUT = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))),
                   'assets', 'charts')

plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.family': 'sans-serif',
    'font.sans-serif': ['PingFang SC', 'Hiragino Sans GB', 'Arial Unicode MS'],
    'axes.unicode_minus': False,
    'text.color': INK, 'axes.labelcolor': DIMC,
    'xtick.color': DIMC, 'ytick.color': DIMC,
    'axes.edgecolor': GRID, 'axes.linewidth': 0.8,
    'font.size': 10,
})


def _clean(ax):
    ax.spines[['top', 'right']].set_visible(False)
    ax.grid(axis='y', color=GRID, linewidth=0.7)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)


def revenue_profit():
    """p2:5 年营收/成本/利润(百万美元,单轴同单位)。"""
    base = F.five_year()
    years = [str(y['year']) for y in base['years']]
    rev = [y['revenue'] / 1e6 for y in base['years']]
    cost = [y['cost'] / 1e6 for y in base['years']]
    profit = [y['profit'] / 1e6 for y in base['years']]
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.4, 3.1), dpi=220)
    w, x = 0.26, range(len(years))
    ax.bar([i - w for i in x], rev, w, color=BLUE, label='营收', edgecolor='white', linewidth=1)
    ax.bar(x, cost, w, color=AMBER, label='成本', edgecolor='white', linewidth=1)
    ax.bar([i + w for i in x], profit, w, color=TEAL, label='利润', edgecolor='white', linewidth=1)
    for i, v in zip(x, profit):
        ax.annotate(f'{v:.0f}', (i + w, v), textcoords='offset points', xytext=(0, 3),
                    ha='center', fontsize=8.5, color=TEAL, fontweight='bold')
    ax.set_xticks(list(x), [f'{y}\nU={u:.0%}' for y, u in
                            zip(years, [yy['utilization'] for yy in base['years']])])
    ax.set_ylabel('百万美元 / 年')
    ax.legend(frameon=False, ncols=3, loc='upper right', fontsize=9)
    _clean(ax)
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(os.path.join(OUT, 'revenue-profit.png'))
    plt.close(fig)


def kv_per_token():
    """p5:各模型每 token KV 字节(注意力架构差异),BF16/FP8 双口径。"""
    rows = [('GLM-5.3\n(78 层 MLA 全增长)', 'glm-5.3'),
            ('DeepSeek-V3 对照\n(61 层 MLA)', None),
            ('Kimi-K3\n(仅 24 层 MLA 增长)', 'kimi-k3'),
            ('DS-V4-Pro\n(CSA/HCA 摊销)', 'dsv4-pro'),
            ('DS-V4-Flash\n(CSA/HCA 摊销)', 'dsv4-flash')]
    bf16, fp8, labels = [], [], []
    for label, key in rows:
        labels.append(label)
        if key is None:  # DeepSeek-V3 基线:61×576 元素(roofline.ts 口径)
            bf16.append(61 * 576 * 2 / 1024)
            fp8.append(61 * 576 * 1 / 1024)
        else:
            bf16.append(C.kv_bytes_per_token(key, 2) / 1024)
            fp8.append(C.kv_bytes_per_token(key, 1) / 1024)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.9, 2.9), dpi=220)
    y = range(len(labels))
    h = 0.32
    ax.barh([i + h / 2 for i in y], bf16, h, color=BLUE, label='KV=BF16(保守)',
            edgecolor='white', linewidth=1)
    ax.barh([i - h / 2 for i in y], fp8, h, color=AMBER, label='KV=FP8(下界)',
            edgecolor='white', linewidth=1)
    for i, v in zip(y, bf16):
        ax.annotate(f'{v:.0f} KB', (v, i + h / 2), textcoords='offset points',
                    xytext=(4, -3), fontsize=8.5, color=BLUE, fontweight='bold')
    ax.set_yticks(list(y), labels, fontsize=8.5)
    ax.invert_yaxis()
    ax.set_xlabel('每 token KV cache(KB,全层合计;官方未声明 KV 精度 → 双口径)')
    ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8.5, loc='lower right')
    ax.spines[['top', 'right']].set_visible(False)
    ax.grid(axis='x', color=GRID, linewidth=0.7)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(os.path.join(OUT, 'kv-per-token.png'))
    plt.close(fig)


def tco_stack():
    """p12:5 年成本构成(折旧/电力/托管/运维)与营收对照。"""
    base = F.five_year()
    years = [str(y['year']) for y in base['years']]
    cb = base['cost_breakdown_y1']
    dep = [cb['dep'] / 1e6] * len(years)
    power = [cb['power'] / 1e6] * len(years)
    colo = [cb['colo'] / 1e6] * len(years)
    ops = [cb['ops'] / 1e6] * len(years)
    rev = [y['revenue'] / 1e6 for y in base['years']]
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.6, 2.7), dpi=220)
    x = range(len(years))
    bottom = [0.0] * len(years)
    for vals, color, label in ((dep, BLUE, 'CapEx 折旧'), (power, AMBER, '电费'),
                               (colo, TEAL, '托管'), (ops, PURPLE, '运维')):
        ax.bar(x, vals, 0.5, bottom=bottom, color=color, label=label,
               edgecolor='white', linewidth=1)
        bottom = [b + v for b, v in zip(bottom, vals)]
    ax.plot(x, rev, color=INK, linewidth=2, marker='o', markersize=5, label='营收')
    ax.set_xticks(list(x), years)
    ax.set_ylabel('百万美元 / 年')
    ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8, ncols=3)
    _clean(ax)
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(os.path.join(OUT, 'tco-stack.png'))
    plt.close(fig)


def main():
    os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
    revenue_profit()
    kv_per_token()
    tco_stack()
    print('charts →', OUT)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

```

# A7 存储架构调研(推理场景四层存储)

访问日期:2026-09-03。侧重推理/RAG 场景(非训练)。所有数字均给出来源;查不到的标 null。

---

## 1. 四层存储总表

| 层 | 承载内容 | 在架构中的位置 | 关键参数量级(已核实) | 影响的业务场景与指标 | 代表产品 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| L1 本地 NVMe | 容器镜像缓存、模型缓存(热模型副本)、KV cache 溢出(G3 盘层)、临时张量/短期日志 | GPU 节点内,PCIe Gen5 直连;NVIDIA 推理 RA 将其定义为"有规划的层级,而非应急溢出" [S5] | 单盘 Gen5 x4:14 GB/s 顺序读 / 10 GB/s 写 / ~2M 随机读 IOPS(Micron 9550、Phison Pascari D200V);单 U.2 最大 245.76 TB(Pascari D206V)[S13][S14];节点 8 盘聚合 ~100 GB/s 量级(推导) | 扩容冷启动(镜像+权重本地命中免网络拉取)、KV 盘层命中→TTFT、节点故障重启速度 | Micron 9550、Phison Pascari、Solidigm 等企业级 Gen5 SSD |
| L2 高性能共享存储 | 热模型仓库(全集群共享一份权重)、数据集、checkpoint、多节点并行读 | 计算网/存储网上的并行 FS 或 NFS 加速层;SuperPOD 认证体系的核心层 | SuperPOD B300 RA:单 SU 读 80 GB/s(Standard)~250 GB/s(Enhanced),写为读的 ~1/2;8 SU 聚合读 640~2,000 GB/s;高负载场景 4 GB/s/GPU 读 [S3];DGX H100 节点 GDS 直读 >40 GB/s(≈5 GB/s/GPU)[S4] | 新模型 T+7 上线(一次落盘、全集群加载)、多副本并发扩容、checkpoint 恢复 | WEKA、VAST、DDN EXAScaler、IBM Storage Scale、Pure FlashBlade(GB200/GB300 SuperPOD 认证)、NetApp [S2][S17] |
| L3 对象存储 | 模型归档/版本库(source of truth)、冷数据、日志、备份 | 存储后端/数据湖;推理 RA:"模型工件通常始于对象或文件存储" [S5] | 高性能对象存储单服务器(NVMe 底座)>100 GB/s;MinIO WARP 集群纪录 23.5 TiB/s;AI 场景要求 100+ Gbps 级吞吐 [S15];公有云单流/单实例通常受 NIC(100~400 Gbps)与并发度限制 | 模型版本管理与回滚、合规留存、成本(冷热分层);拉取吞吐决定"对象层→共享层"的分发时间 | MinIO AIStor、Cloudian、DDN Infinia(对象+元数据,RAG 检索)[S16]、AWS S3 等 |
| L4 数据库与向量存储 | 推理平台 metadata(租户/配额/计费)、RAG 向量索引、企业知识库 | 控制面 + RAG 数据面;NVIDIA AIDP/STX 把 NeMo Retriever、AI-Q、Dynamo 嵌入存储栈做 RAG 加速 [S1] | 向量检索跨网络 p99 约 30–250 ms;优化案例:RAG 管线 p99 1.8 s → 190 ms(组件同机);目标口径 embed+检索+LLM 首包 <50 ms(H100)[S18];GPU 索引(CAGRA)相对 CPU 10–50x QPS [S18] | RAG 端到端 TTFT(检索时延直接串行叠加在 prefill 之前)、知识库规模与新鲜度 | Milvus(+CAGRA)、Qdrant、Weaviate;PostgreSQL/pgvector;Elasticsearch |

容量与 GPU 数的典型配比:**null**——SuperPOD B300 RA 明确不给出每 SU/每 GPU 容量指标 [S3];推理集群公开的权威"TB/GPU"配比未检索到,建议 deck 以"按模型库大小 × 副本数 + KV 盘层预留"自行推导。

---

## 2. 模型加载链路(对象存储 → 共享存储 → 本地 NVMe → HBM)

关联业务指标:「新模型 T+7 上线」与扩容冷启动(scale-out TTFT)。

### 2.1 NVIDIA 推理 RA 的口径 [S5]
- 冷启动应拆解为独立可测阶段:工件发现 → 缓存预热 → 权重搬运 → 容器启动 → 后端初始化 → first-ready。
- 加速组件:Run:ai Model Streamer、ModelExpress、NIXL 等,针对"模型加载/权重搬运/大负载移动"瓶颈。

### 2.2 公开案例(实测数字)
- **Run:ai Model Streamer 官方基准**(Llama-3-8B,15 GB,AWS A10G)[S6]:
  - GP3 SSD(1 GiB/s 上限):HF safetensors 47.99 s → Streamer 14.34 s(打满盘带宽);
  - IO2 SSD(4 GiB/s):47.0 s → 7.53 s;
  - S3:Streamer 4.88 s(并发 32) vs Tensorizer 37.36 s;
  - vLLM 就绪总时间:约 62–66 s(safetensors)→ 23–35 s(Streamer)。
  - 结论:加载时间 ≈ 权重体积 ÷ 存储层可用带宽,前提是加载器能并发打满带宽。
- **Azure Blob + Model Streamer**:冷启动最多快 6x [S7]。
- **70B 级冷启动量级**:70B FP16 ≈ 140 GB;未缓存容器全流程 6–10 分钟,镜像已预拉取时 60–90 s [S8][S9]。
- **DeepSeek-R1 671B**(FP8 ≈ 685 GB VRAM):vLLM 首次启动"数分钟"级,含下载则更久 [S10]。
- **Run:ai GPU memory swap**:对已驻留模型,较 scale-from-zero 快 44–61x TTFT(说明"避免重新加载"比"加速加载"收益更大)[S8]。

### 2.3 750 GB–1.6 TB 权重的时间量级推导(deck 可用)
以 1 TB 权重、单节点 8 GPU 为例(各段按可打满带宽估算):
| 链路段 | 假设带宽 | 时间量级 |
|---|---|---|
| 对象存储 → 共享存储(一次性入库) | 10–50 GB/s(集群聚合) | ~20 s–2 min |
| 共享存储 → 单节点(GDS/并行 FS) | 40 GB/s/节点 [S4] | ~25 s |
| 本地 NVMe → CPU/GPU(8 盘并发) | 50–100 GB/s/节点 | ~10–20 s |
| PCIe Gen5 → HBM(每 GPU 分片 ~125 GB) | ~50–60 GB/s/GPU 实效 | ~2–3 s |
| 引擎初始化(权重解析、CUDA graph、warmup) | — | 数十秒–数分钟 |
关键结论:**存储 I/O 只占冷启动的一部分,加载器并发度与引擎初始化同样是主瓶颈**;N 节点同时扩容时,对象层出口带宽被 ×N 放大,必须靠共享层/本地缓存/节点间 P2P(ModelExpress)吸收。

---

## 3. KV cache 分层(关联推理性能/TTFT)

| 层级 | 介质带宽量级 | 时延量级 | 公开收益数字 | 方案 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| G1:GPU HBM | HBM3e ~8 TB/s/GPU(B200 级,公开规格) | 纳秒–微秒 | 基线 | 各推理引擎原生 |
| G2:CPU DRAM(pinned) | ~0.5 TB/s/socket(DDR5);经 PCIe Gen5 搬运 ~50–60 GB/s/GPU | 微秒 | LMCache:128K 上下文 TTFT 11 s → 1.5 s;多轮 agentic(MI300X)平均 TTFT 3.0x 降低、p95 2.1x [S11] | Dynamo KVBM(G2)、LMCache、Mooncake(DRAM 池化) |
| G3:本地 NVMe | 14 GB/s/盘,节点级几十 GB/s | 几十–百微秒 | KVBM 盘层默认"频次 ≥2 才下盘"以保 SSD 寿命 [S12];NVIDIA 2026 起推动 KV 下放 NVMe 标准化 [S19] | Dynamo KVBM(G3)、vLLM/SGLang HiCache + NIXL |
| G4:远端共享 NVMe(GDS/RDMA) | 厂商宣称多 TB/s 集群聚合、"DRAM 级吞吐" | 百微秒–毫秒 | WEKA AMG:105K token 输入 TTFT 23.97 s → 0.58 s(41x),tokens/GPU 最高 4.2x [S20][S21];VAST+Dynamo(CoreWeave 实测):TTFT 改善 20x、GPU 效率 +90% [S22];Mooncake:模拟场景吞吐最高 +525% [S23] | WEKA Augmented Memory Grid、VAST VUA(开源,vLLM/LMCache/Dynamo 集成)[S24]、Mooncake Store |

口径提醒:41x/20x 这类数字是"长上下文重复命中 vs 全量重算 prefill"的对比,命中率决定实际收益;deck 引用时应写"命中场景下"。

---

## 4. RAG 向量库位置与 TTFT 影响

- 位置:第 4 层数据面;NVIDIA AIDP/STX 趋势是把检索(NeMo Retriever/AI-Q/Dynamo)下沉进存储平台,DDN、IBM、Cloudian、Pure 等均发布对应参考架构 [S1][S16][S17]。
- 典型选型:Milvus(GPU CAGRA 索引,10–50x QPS vs CPU)、Qdrant、Weaviate [S18]。
- 时延口径:检索(embedding + ANN + rerank)串行在 prefill 之前,直接加到 TTFT 上;跨服务部署向量库 p99 约 30–250 ms,叠加 LLM 首包 100–600 ms;同机/同集群优化后整链 p99 可压到 ~190 ms,理想目标 <50 ms [S18]。

# A9 — p10 软件平台/运维/安全 + p11 PoC 与验收 素材

检索日期:2026-09-03(全部 URL 当日经 WebSearch 核实可达)。搜索预算:15 次,已用 15。
标注约定:查证到公开出处的给 URL;业界通行但无单一权威出处的标「通行实践」;查不到的标 null。

---

## P10 素材:运维场景 × 角色矩阵 + AI agent 替代

### 1. 推理平台关键运维场景清单(业界通行说法,出处见矩阵)

模型上线/切换(含灰度/金丝雀)、扩缩容(autoscaling)、故障定位(RCA)、性能回归(版本/驱动升级后)、SLA 看板与告警、安全审计与访问控制、成本优化(FinOps)、容量规划复盘。
- 角色分工佐证:平台工程侧要交付 "Inference-as-a-Service"、抽象 GPU 驱动/模型版本/环境([Itential: Platform Engineering for AI](https://www.itential.com/blog/company/infrastructure-as-code/platform-engineering-for-ai-product-teams));推理服务专职岗负责 serving、延迟预算、金丝雀路由([Scale AI JD: Model Serving Platform](https://scale.com/careers/4520320005)、[GM JD: Inference Platform](https://search-careers.gm.com/en/jobs/jr-202604629/senior-ml-infrastructure-engineer-inference-platform/));FinOps for AI 由 FinOps Foundation 正式立项,覆盖 GPU/token 成本的 Inform-Optimize-Operate 生命周期,2025-11 起有专门认证([FinOps Foundation: FinOps for AI Overview](https://www.finops.org/wg/finops-for-ai-overview/))。

### 2. 场景 × 角色矩阵(含 L0–L4 自动化程度建议)

自动化分级口径(参照 Azure SRE Agent 的 Review/Autonomous 双模式与"policy guardrails + human approval"框架,[Azure SRE Agent Overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sre-agent/overview)):
- **L0** 纯人工;**L1** AI 辅助信息聚合(日志/指标汇总);**L2** AI 给出建议、人执行;**L3** AI 执行、人审批(Review mode);**L4** 护栏内全自主(Autonomous mode)。

| 场景 | 主责角色 | 协作角色 | 今日建议自动化 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 模型上线/切换 | 推理/模型工程师 | 平台工程师、SRE | L2–L3 | 金丝雀+自动回滚可到 L3;新模型选型与放量决策留人 |
| 扩缩容 | SRE | 平台工程师、FinOps | L3–L4 | 指标驱动 autoscaling 是最成熟的自动化项(Azure SRE Agent 可自动 scale) |
| 故障定位(RCA) | SRE | 推理工程师 | L2–L3 | Meta 42% top-5 命中、Datadog/Azure agent 均为"假设-验证"式 RCA;结论仍需人确认 |
| 性能回归(bisect) | 推理/模型工程师 | SRE | L2 | InferenceMAX 每夜跑法可自动发现回归([Tom's Hardware](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/inferencemax-ai-benchmark-tests-software-stacks-efficiency-and-tco-vendor-neutral-suite-runs-nightly-and-tracks-performance-changes-over-time));归因与修复留人 |
| SLA 看板与告警 | SRE | 平台工程师 | L3–L4 | 告警聚合/降噪/初筛是 AI SRE 产品主打(Datadog Bits) |
| 安全审计 | 安全合规 | 平台工程师 | L1–L2 | 日志聚合与异常初筛可自动;审计结论、合规签署必须人 |

## P11 素材:行业标准 PoC 与验收方法

### 1. 标准测试指标定义表

| 指标 | 定义 | 出处 |
|---|---|---|
| **TTFT** | 请求发出到收到首 token 的时间;含排队、prefill、网络延迟 | [NVIDIA GenAI-Perf 文档](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/triton-inference-server/user-guide/docs/perf_analyzer/genai-perf/README.html)、[NVIDIA: LLM Benchmarking Fundamental Concepts](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/llm-benchmarking-fundamental-concepts/) |
| **ITL / TPOT** | 相邻输出 token 平均间隔;GenAI-Perf 公式:ITL = (e2e_latency − TTFT) / (总输出 token − 1),不含 TTFT | 同上;[AIPerf Metrics Reference](https://docs.nvidia.com/aiperf/reference/ai-perf-metrics-reference) |
| **E2E 请求延迟** | 提交到完整响应,含排队/批处理/网络 | [NIM Benchmarking Metrics](https://docs.nvidia.com/nim/benchmarking/llm/latest/metrics.html) |
| **吞吐** | output tokens/s(系统级常用 tok/s/GPU)与 requests/s | 同上 |
| **交互性** | tok/s/user(单用户流速),与 tok/s/GPU 构成两难 | [InferenceX Glossary: Pareto frontier](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/glossary/pareto-frontier) |
| **Goodput** | 满足 SLO(如 p99 TTFT/TPOT 约束、≥99% 达标率)前提下的每秒完成请求数 | 概念出自 DistServe(OSDI'24):[论文 PDF](https://www.usenix.org/system/files/osdi24-zhong-yinmin.pdf)、[arXiv 2401.09670](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.09670v1) |
| **吞吐-延迟 / Pareto 曲线** | 扫并发得 tok/s/GPU × tok/s/user 曲线;剔除被支配点后的有效边界;评估应比整条曲线而非单点 | [InferenceMAX: Open Source Inference Benchmarking](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/blog/inferencemax-open-source-inference-benchmarking)、[NVIDIA Blackwell on InferenceMAX v1](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/nvidia-blackwell-leads-on-new-semianalysis-inferencemax-benchmarks/) |

**MLPerf Inference(datacenter)对 LLM 的标准测法**:TTFT/TPOT 作为延迟约束,测约束内最大可持续吞吐。
- Llama 2 70B **Server** 场景:TTFT ≤ 2 s、TPOT ≤ 200 ms([MLCommons 2024](https://mlcommons.org/2024/03/mlperf-llama2-70b/));
- v5.0 新增 **Interactive** 场景:TTFT ≤ 450 ms、TPOT ≤ 40 ms([MLCommons v5.0](https://mlcommons.org/2025/04/llm-inference-v5/));
- v5.1 增 Llama 3.1-8B:CNN-DailyMail 数据集,平均 ISL 778 / OSL 73([MLCommons v5.1](https://mlcommons.org/2025/09/small-llm-inference-5-1/))。
- InferenceMAX 与之互补:开源、每夜自动运行、跟踪软件栈演进与 TCO([Tom's Hardware](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/inferencemax-ai-benchmark-tests-software-stacks-efficiency-and-tco-vendor-neutral-suite-runs-nightly-and-tracks-performance-changes-over-time);后更名 InferenceX,[v2 报告](https://newsletter.semianalysis.com/p/inferencex-v2-nvidia-blackwell-vs))。

### 2. PoC 七步流程要点(拼自公开方法论,单一"验收签署模板":null)

最接近的公开模板:[NVIDIA NIM LLM Latency-Throughput Benchmarking 指南](https://docs.nvidia.com/nim/benchmarking/llm/latest/index.html)(定指标→起服务→预热→单用例→用例扫描→分析)与 [Together AI: GPU 集群测试运行实践指南](https://www.together.ac/blog/a-practitioners-guide-to-testing-and-running-large-gpu-clusters-for-training-generative-ai-models)(注:正确域名为 together.ai)。

1. **需求对齐**:业务 SLA 定成 TTFT/TPOT(或 tok/s/user)+ 达标率(通行实践,指标口径见上表)。
2. **Workload 画像**:ISL/OSL 分布、并发、到达率、prefix 重合度——NIM 指南要求按 use case(翻译/摘要/生成等各有典型 ISL/OSL)分别测;MLPerf 用真实数据集定 ISL/OSL 同理。
3. **环境准备与烤机**:上生产负载前先做节点 burn-in + NCCL 全网收敛测试(单机→成对→分组→全集群),环境变量对齐生产配置([Together AI 指南](https://www.together.ai/blog/a-practitioners-guide-to-testing-and-running-large-gpu-clusters-for-training-generative-ai-models)、[Crusoe burn-in 实践](https://www.crusoe.ai/resources/blog/how-crusoe-burn-in-tests-every-node-before-it-reaches-you)、[Leviathan: NCCL Bandwidth Validation](https://www.leviathansystems.co/articles/nccl-bandwidth-validation))。
4. **基准测试**:GenAI-Perf/AIPerf 扫并发,得吞吐-延迟全曲线与 Pareto 边界(出处同指标表)。
5. **SLA 验证**:以 goodput 口径复测——SLO 约束下 p99 达标(DistServe,出处同上)。
6. **故障演练**:节点故障/降级下的恢复与 SLA 保持(通行实践;Azure SRE Agent 文档的事件响应流程可作参照,单独的推理侧公开 chaos checklist:null)。
7. **验收签署**:双方按第 1 步 SLA + 第 4-6 步证据签字(通行实践;公开签署模板:null)。

### 3. 常见坑清单(带出处)

| # | 坑 | 说明与出处 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **只测峰值吞吐不看 goodput** | 高吞吐可伴随大量 SLO 违约;DistServe 证明按 goodput 优化可差出数倍成本([OSDI'24](https://www.usenix.org/system/files/osdi24-zhong-yinmin.pdf));InferenceMAX 明确反对单点吞吐、主张全 Pareto 曲线([方法论](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/blog/inferencemax-open-source-inference-benchmarking)) |
| 2 | **Prompt 分布与生产不符** | 不同 use case 的 ISL/OSL 差异巨大,须按用例分测(NIM 指南 "Sweeping through use cases",[docs](https://docs.nvidia.com/nim/benchmarking/llm/latest/index.html));MLPerf 亦按真实数据集固定分布 |
| 3 | **Prefix cache 命中率虚高** | 命中率强依赖 workload:多轮对话 ~90.7% vs 摘要 6.3% vs 代码补全 0.1%;应按 workload 单独报,不能拿会话型 benchmark 的命中率外推([llm-d: KV-Cache Wins You Can See](https://llm-d.ai/blog/kvcache-wins-you-can-see);另见 [BentoML Handbook: Prefix caching](https://bentoml.com/llm/inference-optimization/prefix-caching):prompt 微小变化即失效) |
| 4 | **烤机/浸泡时长不足** | 短时合成 burn-in 只能抓硬故障,抓不到持续性能退化与显存带宽/NVLink/PCIe 路径问题;需长时真实负载浸泡([Guard, arXiv 2605.17879](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.17879);[Together AI 指南](https://www.together.ai/blog/a-practitioners-guide-to-testing-and-running-large-gpu-clusters-for-training-generative-ai-models)) |
| 5 | **投机解码在真实流量下接受率下降** | 官方加速数常在 batch 1–4、高接受率区间测得;真实分布下接受率约 0.6–0.8,加速缩水,且与结构化输出/reasoning parser 组合有静默丢 token 风险;须按流量分段监控接受率([Speculative Decoding in Production: Hidden Traps](https://tianpan.co/blog/2026-04-17-speculative-decoding-production-hidden-traps);[vLLM Discussion #13834](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/discussions/13834);[BentoML Handbook](https://bentoml.com/llm/inference-optimization/speculative-decoding)) |
| 6 | **Reasoning 模型 TTFT 口径混淆** | 引擎层 TTFT 应量到**首个 reasoning token**;用户体感应看"首个 answer token"(思考之后)——两个口径可差一个完整思考段,PoC 须写明用哪个([NVIDIA: LLM Benchmarking Fundamental Concepts](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/llm-benchmarking-fundamental-concepts/);[Artificial Analysis 方法论](https://artificialanalysis.ai/methodology/performance-benchmarking) 的 "Time to First Answer Token") |
